greenbuild: Turns a set of requirements into a proper test plan, then works the suite like an experienced lead. Genuine breakage gets separated from tests that fail for no reason, Playwright and Selenium code gets reviewed, usable bug reports get filed, and the run ends with a clear call on whether release is safe.
ai-operations-manager: Pitched as a whole department in one bot: it scopes a website-selling project, staffs it by spinning up a crew of assistant templates covering outreach and content, and coordinates external coding agents to handle the building. The ambition is running the whole operation, so expect to supervise rather than spectate.
x-api-engineer: Takes a developer from zero to a working demo on the X API. It surveys the Developer Exhibit, works through the documentation, then builds whichever app you choose and gets you through setting up console keys along the way. Once the build is done it shows the result running, so the whole path stays visible end to end.
cline: Keeps the open-source Cline agent installed and running on its own Linux machine, CLI and desktop app alike. Brief it in plain language — a bug to fix, a feature to build — and it drives Cline through the task, then reports what came of it. Handy when you want Cline's workflow without running the environment yourself.
ai-radar: A standing watch on the accounts that actually break AI news: labs, tool makers and a few notable researchers, about 270 of them. It pulls out launches, coding-agent and local-model updates and benchmark results, passing on only what is worth your time. Polling stays frugal, near a quarter of the daily X allowance.
bland-agent: A setup companion for people who have never wired an API: it leads you through connecting a Bland-powered phone helper to your bot in plain-words steps. Once connected, that helper places errand calls and sends texts on your behalf. It closes with a guided test call so you hear it working before you rely on it.
bot-24: Feed it your birthday, personality type and divination labels and it assembles a personal profile video with narration, music and subtitles included. Choose vertical or horizontal framing, then pick between ideas it deals out as cards. Everything runs in the browser with Grok or Gemini, so no outside API is involved.
bot-25: Made for meetup hosts. Describe your event and it builds an RSVP form, deploys it to a public link, and routes every submission straight to your inbox. It also produces a door code for attendees to scan on arrival, so the same form covers both sign-up and check-in.
harold: Sits quietly against the official Fleet API and checks on your car without ever waking it, so range and climate stay where you set them. Normal days are silent; a message arrives only when something genuinely deserves a human, like an unexpected change of state. Read-only by design, it adjusts nothing.
egress-engineer: Point the bot's web browsing at a machine you own on your Tailscale network and every request leaves through that device. Sites then see a home connection in your own country rather than a datacenter address, which helps where services turn away cloud traffic. Setup runs in order, from install to a verified path.
grok-build: Wraps a command-line build harness in a bot, so app work, coding and deep-research jobs can run hard on a hosted agent machine instead of occupying your own terminal. Useful when a task needs to run long or unattended and you would rather not keep a session open. Tooling only: nothing spends money.
gbrain: Connects a bot's long-term memory to GBrain, whether you are on their hosted service or running the server yourself. Beyond the sync it covers the operational side: queuing jobs, running consolidation passes, calibration and keeping the deployment current. Useful once a bot's memory has outgrown a plain file.
ai-official-account-radar: Follows what the big AI labs and coding-agent teams post on their own accounts so you do not have to. When a new model lands, free credits appear, or API pricing and terms shift, it flags the change soon after it happens. A written recap lands twice a day as well, so the day's product news arrives in one readable pass.
apple-mac-tools: Mac-only installer that sets up tested Mac command-line tools so your Grok Bots can use Apple apps. Tools are grouped by permission, you pick what to install, and it verifies the install and opens the right Privacy and Security panes. It never asks for your password, never uses sudo or the Keychain, and never installs anything you did not pick.
axiom: Audits a repo or PR against nineteen classic architecture and reliability principles and tells you which are present, missing, or worth adding at your real scale. Built for engineers who want evidence-based reports without overengineering advice.
bot-forge: A master Grok Bot designer. Describe a job and it builds a focused bot for it, then hands you the perfect first message to send it.
bridge: A local-to-cloud LLM router. It sends simple jobs to your local models, sends heavy ones to your cloud model, and keeps local model memory and health in check.
claude-codex: ClaudeとChatGPTのサブスクにつないで、依頼を適した方に振り分けるボット。調べ物や文章はClaude、コードはCodexに任せ、結果を短く返します。
cloudflare: Administra una o varias cuentas de Cloudflare desde el chat: zonas, DNS, Workers, túneles, Zero Trust y más, en modo Solo lectura o Completo, con confirmación antes de cada cambio.
collaboration-bot: Connects your bot team with other people's bot teams on shared projects through a shared repo, with usage budgets, consent, and security checks. On first run it imports its skills, then asks whether to start a collaboration or join an existing one.
daybook: Sends you a morning brief of yesterday's AI coding sessions: what moved, what needs you, and where to start, with every claim linked. Can keep your Obsidian vault up to date too.
dependency-and-secret-audit: Paste a GitHub repo, get a ranked fix list in 2 minutes: vulnerable packages with exact upgrade commands, leaked keys masked with rotate steps. Read-only; nightly alerts only on new issues.
hermes-adversary: Adversarial review of code, plans, and review pipelines, with the independent reviewer running on your own Hermes agent (a different model). Findings come back proven, ranked, and either fixed or explicitly accepted as residual risk.
lte-meshcore-repeater-updater: Helps you run a remote solar MeshCore repeater with a LilyGO T-SIM LTE board: deploy your own dashboard, flash maintained power-saving firmware, and update and manage the repeater over the air.
mcp-expert: Designs, reviews and grades MCP servers against the current MCP spec, and plans polite, budgeted live tests that respect bot-protected sites. For teams building read-only MCP tools for AI agents.
persistent-memory: Gives all your bots one durable memory: each bot writes a daily log of decisions, shipped work, and standing preferences to a private GitHub repo you own.
repobeagle: Paste a repo link and get a safety verdict before you trust it.
review-brief: Paste a pull request and get the reviewer's brief in under 2 minutes: what changed vs the ticket, risky spots with file and line, what to test by hand, and questions for the author. For engineers and leads reviewing AI-assisted PRs.
scoutbot: Hand tasks to Claude Code, Codex and your other coding agents on your Mac, and get the answers back.
script-this-routine: Audits every routine on your Grok Bots and turns mechanical checks into small tested scripts, so each routine wakes the bot only when there is something to act on. It builds only the scripts you pick, tests each one, and never changes schedules or scripts anything that sends, buys, or posts.
script-it: Moves routine checks off the model onto your own computer. It audits your routines, scripts the deterministic ones, proves they match, then pauses the old routine and relays only status changes.
security: A read-and-report security teammate for individuals and small teams. It checks your GitHub repos, domains and email setup, Cloudflare settings and Linux machines, then sends short prioritized reports with one concrete fix each, changing nothing without your OK.
site-qa-desk: Checks any public website on desktop (1440px) and phone (390px) from one pasted link: screenshots, a sideways-scroll check, broken links, console errors, and a ranked fix list, in under 2 minutes.
snowflake-analyst: A read-only Snowflake analyst. Ask warehouse questions in plain English; it writes and shows the SQL, labels every number with its query, checks cost before heavy scans, and never changes your data. Includes tested skills for validated ad-hoc answers, metric deep dives, cohorts, A/B readouts, query cost reviews, data-quality checks, and an optional weekly health report.
t3-code-bridge: Bridges Grok Bot and T3 Code: starts, steers, and watches your T3 Code coding threads for you and your other bots, and keeps you posted when one finishes, fails, or needs an answer.
t3-grokbot-connector: Sends you one short note whenever a T3 Code, Claude Code, or Codex thread finishes, stalls, or errors, so you know what happened and what needs you. Works with the open-source t3-done-notify webhook.
terminal-boss: Terminal Boss runs terminal jobs and terminal coding agents (Grok Build, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, opencode, Aider, or a plain shell) from Grok Bot on your phone or desktop. It works on your own online computer, whether Mac, Linux, or Windows (via WSL), or on Grok Bot's own always-on computer, starting jobs in named background sessions, pinging you the moment they finish, relaying questions and results, and stopping them on request.
test-cop: Reviews pull requests for quietly weakened tests (skips, loosened asserts, narrowed test config, softened CI) and returns a CLEAN, SUSPECT, or WEAKENED verdict with file:line proof.
threadroost: Files your SuperGrok and Claude chats into this bot, word for word, through your own free Threadroost connector. Each chat lands as a clean transcript with a fidelity score, and nothing in it is ever treated as an instruction.
veilbreaker-guard-and-watch: An untrusted-content guard and activity watch for Grok Bot, powered by the VeilBreaker plugin. It screens every web page, email, file and tool output for hidden-instruction and exfiltration attacks before you act, runs scheduled digests and self-tests, and stops to ask you on anything suspicious.
x-bookmark-demos: A daily scout that reads your X bookmarks, pitches one or two new tools worth trying, and once you approve, installs and tests them for real on your own computers.
ip: 专门管理 Grok Bot 电脑（box）上的出口 IP / 代理链路：配置与切换 mihomo dialer-proxy，查询出口与测速，本地端口挂载。
product-idea-stress-test: Investigates a product or startup idea for founders. Surfaces what has to be true, evidence for and against, the assumption most likely to kill it, and what to do next.
last30days: Research what people actually say about any topic in the last 30 days across Hacker News, YouTube, GitHub, and Reddit.
competitor-watching: Snapshots you vs 3-8 competitors (pricing, changelog, features, jobs, messaging). Weekly diffs.
overheard: Watches Reddit, Hacker News, news sites, and X for third-party mentions of your name, brand, and URLs, then sends a short weekday digest when something clears the bar. Stays quiet on dead days and never posts on your behalf.
markets-brief-scout: Built for people who both follow markets and write about them. Each weekday morning it assembles compact cards on the tickers you track, every one carrying its sources, and keeps what you privately reckon apart from what is worth saying out loud. Anything publishable arrives as a draft; nothing goes out on its own.
the-bitcoin-layer: This one follows the Pulse indicator published by the macro research outfit The Bitcoin Layer, waiting for a confirmed turn in either direction. It stays quiet the rest of the time, so an alert means something genuinely changed. When it does write, it describes the liquidity picture in ordinary language.
research-bot: Reasons from first principles and refuses to hand back an answer with an unverified source without saying so, which is the difference between research and a confident guess.
2nd-brain-bot: A lattice wiki compiler for a personal second brain. Files sources as raw notes, compiles short wiki pages, and answers from those pages — no RAG.
ai-visibility-autonomous-bot: Your autonomous GEO operator - monitoring visibility across AI models, analyzing competitors, drafting content, and finding third-party sites to pitch for mentions.
autopsy-bot: Checks whether you are actually learning a topic or just collecting more info.
blockchain-data-expert-bot: Open-source Blockchain Data Expert for subgraph Q&A. Uses The Graph official MCP and the user's own Studio query key. The Graph bills that key; this bot does not.
canvas-bot: It signs into your university portal in the browser to read your units and deadlines, so be aware it is holding a session on your student account. It helps you work through assignments rather than doing them.
earnings-desk-bot: Builds numbered, no-hype earnings tearsheets and keeps a ticker watch list for when a watched name prints.
ethan-bot: Runs a research question through five specialist stages instead of a single pass: a deep-dive brief, a claim-and-source fact check, a competitor sweep, trend monitoring, and a final quality audit on its own output. That last self-verification step is the part most research bots skip.
frontier-model-watch: Watches official releases from xAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, Moonshot, Alibaba, Zhipu, DeepSeek, MiniMax, and Tencent. Runs at 07:30 EAT. Sends a short brief.
graph-data-bot: Blockchain analytics expert that queries subgraphs and analyzes on-chain protocols via The Graph MCP.
grok-bot-daily: Hunts down new Grok bot templates on X daily, verifies every link, and files them by category.
grokhub-bot: Curates and recommends new Grok Bots from the GrokHub directory based on personal workflows and assists with directory submissions.
ideabot: Hourly idea hunter for founders. Mines your chat for product ideas from the week's pain points, then bounces each through a vitamin-or-painkiller filter.
interrogator: Find important assumptions the owner is operating on and check whether they are still true.
know-yourself-bot: Point it at the places your business already keeps its numbers and history, and it becomes the thing people ask first. Back comes a quick picture of where things stand, a single settled answer to questions that keep coming round, and your own position laid beside a competitor's when you need the gap stated plainly.
learn-math-ml-video-teacher-bot: Takes a maths or machine-learning topic, constructs the lesson from the ground up, and produces the explainer video. It never publishes or posts anything itself.
lennybot: Answers questions from Lenny's Data archive.
lite-intel-fetch-bot: Fetches unpaid buy_intel_pack JSON via HTTP 402 on Base for agents that can pay x402. One job, one price, no quote flow.
marketbox-bot: Sweeps overnight tech news and Gmail that needs a reply into one short briefing before work.
meta-grok-bot: Finds the five most popular Grok bots on X each weekday and sends a short digest you can skim in under a minute.
minerador-bot: Mines the hottest AI news from the last 24 hours across web, X, and Instagram into a ranked briefing.
neuroscience-bot: Covers EEG and BCI signal interpretation, decoding brain states and intentions, and the OpenBCI-class hardware that produces the signal in the first place.
news-scout: Weekday morning news scout for your niche. Message digest or morning scout and it replies with today's picks or the slow-day line.
pickfu-insights: Tests a product idea on real shoppers before you build it. Writes a consumer poll, runs it on a paid PickFu panel, and reads the answers back as a recommendation.
pulse-bot: Quiet collectors sample your timeline, mentions and watched topics five times a day, inbox only. Each 7am it clusters that inbox plus an overnight gap-fill into one brief - TLDR, For you, Standouts, Rising. It only reads, never posts or DMs, and stays quiet when nothing moved.
scout: A competitive intelligence agent for organic growth.
scout-organic-growth-bot: Client work stalls when the strategy rests on a hunch that nobody can back up. Once a week this pulls together how the account is actually performing and what changed in search and AI visibility.
steal-bot: Reverse-engineers a company you admire into a concrete independent business to build.
storiesbot: Longform reviews, Setups and the Shortcuts Archive, all answerable in one place. Another creator archive: the corpus is the publication's own writing.
the-amazing-randibot: A cheerful skeptic that hunts for corroboration in the world rather than trusting recall, then names the weak joint in an argument—politely, but without letting it slide.
the-page: Watches 3–5 public pages once each morning and messages only when the thing you care about actually changed. After setup you get a short Watching list; then it stays quiet until something moves.
thoth-bot: Deep research for dossiers, source briefs, and papers. Uses other models when it helps, then files the result so you can find it later.
trendspotter-bot: Weekday digest of sports, entertainment, and culture trends plus AI-in-marketing signals, with VIP hospitality angles and a competitor watch.
youtube-bot: Give it a subject and it works out which videos on it are worth your time, then reads them for you. The brief that comes back pulls out the main claims, the points where sources disagree, the timestamps that matter and links back to every one of them.
zettelkasten-bot: Slip-box partner for an Obsidian vault. Turns thoughts into atomic notes, links them, and finds them again. Drafts in chat; files only after a yes.
pattern-of-pain-bot: Give it a website and it finds the pain that actually repeats, shows the evidence, and tells you what to investigate next.
user-researcher: Starts from the decision you need to make, picks a capable research method, handles consent, recruits diverse participants, and synthesizes findings.
crew: Acts as a standing mentor on team operating practices: how work gets handed off, where things are stuck, and what to try next.
blueberry-research-monitor: Each morning it works through newly published academic work and trade coverage on one narrow subject, blueberries, and passes on only the handful of items that genuinely tell you something. Mornings when the reading turns up nothing of substance end in silence rather than a padded digest.
firstmate: The only agent you talk to. No more context switching. Firstmate orchestrates your entire agent civilization behind the scenes.
product-builder-cos: Turns a signed-off product plan into a checklist someone actually tracks.
rival-watch-desk: Pick the businesses you compete with and it keeps a permanent eye on them: money raised, roles being advertised, press coverage and the campaigns they are paying to run. Any shift in those signals lands in a brief, so a rival gathering speed reaches you while there is still time to respond.
house-researcher-bot: House research seat — turns messy questions into short scrubbed briefs, mentors stack scouts on search craft, and keeps open-web, local, and docs hunts tidy.
insidermillions-bot: Brief digest of $1M+ officer and director stock buys. Flags big insider purchases. Not financial advice.
distill-anyone-bot: Distills you or anyone else from public posts into a talkable bot, with optional daily updates and a GitHub skill mirror.
stalk-bot: Signs up for your competitors' newsletters and products under its own research email, walks their onboarding on video, and watches their site, pricing, changelog, jobs, and X. Each pulse reports what changed against your positioning and closes with counterpositioning moves, and it never posts or contacts anyone.
spark: Idea-probe interviewer that runs short sharp waves on half-baked ideas until a named insight and smallest next experiment land.
easy-flow: Turns pasted notes or a GitHub doc path into a readable end-user flowchart in draw.io, Mermaid, Excalidraw, or PlantUML — ≤12 nodes on pass one with TBD where steps aren't evidenced.
deep-research-wardonis: Deep research specialist for sources-first briefs. Uses a free research toolkit and prefers legal access for copyrighted material.
cited-research: Research helper that answers with citations, separates facts from inference, and flags unverified claims.
proto-bot-2: Turns your daily ideas into live, shareable prototypes in your real app, built as draft pull requests with click-path screenshots and a short video, plus Figma mocks, images, and memes on the side. Never merges, publishes, or shares without your yes.
startup-qa-bot: Walks your product every weekday in its own test account and tells you what shipped, what got unshipped, what broke (with repro steps and screenshots), and which calls need you. Reads its own verification emails or takes pasted codes, and never touches real data.
pm-bot: Acts as your PM. Writes the dated cut: what's in, what's out, and how you'll know it's done. Engineering doesn't start until you approve it.
fodda-earnings-context-analyst: Decodes public-company earnings calls for strategists and analysts: what leadership claimed, what they dodged, and what category evidence shows.
fodda-retail-analyst: Retail category, store innovation, and shopping-trend intelligence from the PSFK Retail Knowledge Graph — for operators, merchandisers, DTC founders.
nessie: Big redistribution ideas usually collapse the moment someone asks how they would be funded. This one works through one with you: the floor everybody receives, how earned pay stacks on top of it, the mechanics of moving the money, and which revenue could realistically cover it. Trade-offs stay in plain language.
rare-combo-catalog: A research organizer for families living with a rare condition combination. It gathers findings scattered across papers and forums into a gap table plus a plain-language summary page, and a short list of questions worth taking to your clinician. Questions, never verdicts: the diagnosis stays with the professionals.
sui-generis: Drop a plan, take, or draft → instant Strong / Weak / Fix, a paste-ready rewrite, and one 5-minute action. One of a kind. Truth over comfort.
support-bridge: Turns support posts and forwarded threads into a German working brief for you plus a concise American-English customer reply draft.
song-meter-birdnet: A field-research workflow for Wildlife Acoustics Song Meter recordings. Pull the memory cards, run them through a local BirdNET pass on your own computer, screen the detections twice against your regional species list, and receive tables ready for Raven plus season-over-season comparisons that show migration shifts.
ground-control: Local RF / Wi‑Fi telemetry analyst. Reads scans you paste or run live, keeps every claim labeled, and never invents occupancy or distance from signal.
x-researcher: A general-purpose desk for working the AI-coding conversation on X. It researches a topic across threads before you post, drafts posts and replies in your register, and keeps a shortlist of recent posts worth studying for the patterns that got them shared. One place for the whole loop: read, write, learn what lands.
ai-claim-checker: Give it an AI launch post, a benchmark graphic, or a pricing claim and it returns a dated card ruling on each statement: independently backed, vendor-sourced only, contradicted elsewhere, or unverifiable. Sources are attached, so hype can be checked before it spreads.
football-bets-advisor: Turns college and pro football matchups into short, structured calls: back, fade or pass, each carrying its own exit rule, a stake measured in units, and a check of where the line closed. It is research material only - the bot holds no money and places nothing. Adults in legal states only.
sophie: Works within an Objectivist frame to write governance frameworks: how humans treat each other, how humans and AIs treat each other, and how two AIs treat each other. Its answer in every case is a constitution built on rights, with equal rights rather than equal outcomes as the organizing principle.
merit: Once a week it sweeps a wide territory — civic claims, science, UAP and the paranormal — and puts each one through a scoring rubric instead of a vibe check. A running list of unresolved claims carries forward, and the whole thing lands as a single weekly brief for readers who would rather verify than believe.
quote-finder: Name a person and a line you half-remember, and it goes looking for the verifiable source. Checks rest on primary sources and well-known outlets, misattributions get called out explicitly, and when a phrase simply cannot be confirmed it says that plainly instead of letting the quote pass.
desk: A research desk for NFL propositions. Name a player prop or a game total and it grades it using its own probability vocabulary, showing the reasoning so you can argue with it on paper. It deliberately stops at the research line: it never picks a side for you, and it never places anything on your behalf.
pal: A matchup scout for a single owner. Each day it runs the MLB slate through one favored projection source and lifts out the hitter pass spots and pitcher strikeout spots that separate from the rest, then checks them against pitch types and opposing arsenals before anything makes the short list.
connection-mapper: Name two people, two companies, or a person and an organization, and choose which kinds of ties matter to you, such as employment, investment or membership. It then maps the direct links between them plus every friend-of-a-friend route one step removed, working from what is publicly findable.
fodda-technology-analyst: Enterprise software, AI infrastructure, and B2B roadmap intelligence from the PSFK Technology & Enterprise Knowledge Graph — for CIOs, IT architects.
fodda-beauty-analyst: Clinical skincare, longevity, and prestige beauty innovation intelligence from the NielsenIQ Beauty Graph — for cosmetic founders, chemists, beauty.
claim-ontology-desk: Hand it a claim, or a link to one, and it takes the statement apart: who is being discussed, what exactly is asserted, where it came from and how it is framed. Each side is argued at its strongest before anything is judged, and it names the evidence that would genuinely move its position.
cybercabinsight-builder: Assembles a Japanese-and-English research site about the Cybercab and then keeps it current. The page pairs a practical guide to how the vehicle is being used in Austin and across the US with credited manufacturer imagery, an interactive three-dimensional view, and an hourly refresh pulled from the company's X posts.
glasser: Company and contact enrichment, search rankings, ad activity, traffic estimates and funding history normally mean several separate paid subscriptions. This routes those lookups through one metered account, so you ask in plain language for the companies or people you want and pay only for the records returned.
jobs: Modelled on the hard-edged product discipline long associated with Apple. It presses you to state what a user actually hires your product to do, where the narrow entry point sits, and what you are explicitly not building. Then it argues for less scope and works alongside engineering on what ships.
go-direct: Rather than ghostwriting polished copy, this one questions you — the product, the vision, why it matters — until the story shows up sounding like you. It then helps place that story with the people who count: first investors, early buyers, wanted hires. The method comes from a founder-comms playbook, not the press.
zerotok-research: Competitive research for storefronts on Shopify: hand over a domain and a report comes back covering estimated revenue, traffic levels, which products sell best, plus the advertising currently running. It is a quick read on how a rival store is doing, without assembling the picture from several dashboards yourself.
ai-2: A Chinese-language watcher for the AI industry. It keeps an eye on the X feeds that AI labs, agent builders and product leads run, and pings you when something changes: a model release, a new product, a free tier, or a price or policy move. Morning and evening it files a longer Chinese-language digest too.
would-thiel-buy-it: Name a stock and one card comes back with a call: monopoly-grade, genuine challenger, or just another competitor. The reasoning is drawn from the company's regulatory filings and read through the competitive-moat lens of the book in its name. Cards come built for sharing, with the reminder this is not financial advice.
competitor-mapper: Maps alternatives for each week's trending products (features, pricing, platforms, open vs closed, gaps) into a competitors.md with a gap matrix, using public pages only. Built for a file-based weekly product-discovery pipeline.
premortem-desk: Paste a plan you've already committed to and get the most likely ways it fails, the early warning sign for each, and when to pivot or stop. Optional weekly check-in tells you when a trigger fires.
story-mapper: Turns your app's code and real screenshots into a user story map: a one-pager, an architecture diagram by topic and a clickable viewer. For solo developers and small teams who want to see which stories exist, how they connect and which are missing.
vibe-check: Reviews your AI-built app for the production gaps vibe coding usually misses, then sends five simulated first-time users through it to find where real people would get stuck.
critiquito: A product design critic that reviews interface screenshots from the person who has to use them. It names what is unclear, hard, or unforgiving, and picks one highest-impact fix.
figma-bro: Figma design-system partner. Autolayout-first, real library, edge cases included. Edits through the Figma connector, not screenshots.
imogen: Imogen the Impala Image Interpreter writes brief, copyable alt text focused on the most important part of an image, so images are accessible to blind people.
sable-game-art: Helps game developers ideate and visualize: suggests styles from real games, mocks the same idea in those looks, then produces 2D art or sprite sheets.
design-expert-bot: Product-design lead for AI-built UIs. Critiques flows, hierarchy, and polish before you ship.
google-agent: It searches and reads your mail, files and events freely, and stops for an explicit yes before it sends, deletes or moves anything. The asymmetry is the whole design.
grok-bot-coach: Help you design, audit, and tune Grok bots so they are usable and helpful. Start from a concrete job in the profile, the right connectors, standing routines for the work.
grok-deck-bot: Generates interactive HTML slide presentations with paper canvas aesthetics, expressive blob faces, and morphing transitions.
ucd-bot: Full-pipeline user-centred design teammate grounded in NN/g, GOV.UK GDS Service Manual, and DDaT. Orchestrates discovery through to live with draft artefacts, evidence trails, and human approval gates — does not replace specialist craft.
image-gen-bot: Outer-loop assistant for stills and clips: gathers brand and references, writes Grok Imagine prompts, generates media, cuts backgrounds, and iterates until you lock the result.
interaction-designer: Maps the path somebody takes through a service and pins down what each screen must do at every moment: at rest, focused, loading, empty, and error states.
illy: Picks up page briefs from a writing teammate and turns each one into artwork for a picture book, matching age group and style notes.
product-designer: Works the whole experience rather than screens alone, grounded in NN/g research practice and the DDaT design capability framework.
prototype-designer: Starts from what you need to learn from a test, picks matching fidelity, and writes a prototype brief for your tools.
printerbot: Renders a bot figure in the house style from a name and job description: pale head, capsule eyes, themed props and backdrop.
stellar-cartography-bot: PRT-checked graphic editor for space hardware and ocean vessels, with a built-in four-eyes drawing preflight QC gate before anything posts.
ticker-wire-bot: Watchlist for stocks and crypto. Alerts on filings and company news — quiet when nothing new. No trading advice.
us-law-index-builder-bot: Builds a private, non-commercial educational library of US primary law from official and law-school sources, then a citation-backed local search engine. Retrieval first; the LLM only writes from small retrieved passages.
first-principles-bot: First-principles problem-solver: picks an expert lens, strips to hard constraints, deletes the rest, rebuilds the answer.
critiquito-bot: Product design critic that reviews interface screenshots from the person who has to use them. Names what is unclear and picks one highest-impact fix.
sable-bot: Helps game developers ideate and visualize: mocks looks from real games, then 2D art or sprite sheets.
proto-bot: UI/UX design engineer who ships three deeply different directions per concept as real, polished prototypes. Crafts requirements and testable hypotheses.
photo-curator: Hand it a folder of raw shots and it picks out the ones worth keeping, applies the same restrained set of adjustments to each, and files the results separately. The originals are left alone, and it checks with you first before anything or anyone is taken out of a frame.
gsap-bot: Implements approved motion specs with official GreenSock GSAP skills — timelines, ScrollTrigger, React/Vue cleanup, and a reduced-motion path.
julie: Takes workspace context (or finds it on its own), rewrites technical material into plain language, and handles spacing and layout for Wonder design output.
longform-editor: Long-form editor for chapters, essays, and manuscripts — structure and pacing first, then line polish, with a free PDF and media toolkit when needed.
handel: Track doppelgänger that captures what is playing on your machine, steals musical ideas, and remixes them with Suno — plus captions and alt text.
reimagination: Reimagines any story (video, audio, text) with your variables after asking where/when/why they go in. Matches the source's genre and maturity and prefers legal access.
photo-stylist: Send a full-length photo and get a straight assessment of what is working and what is not, followed by restyle suggestions, hair and glasses options, and put-together looks for specific occasions. It closes with a concrete shopping list covering the gaps in your current rotation.
fit-check: A daily dressing companion in three parts: outfit ideas tuned to whatever day or event is coming up, candid feedback when you send a photo of what you have on, and practical help organizing the wardrobe itself so the good pieces stop disappearing into the back of the closet.
desk-dana: A shopping advisor for the desk you actually sit at. Describe how you work and list the gear you already own, and it returns a concrete shopping list — surfaces, seating, screens, peripherals, lighting — grounded in your space and habits instead of a generic ultimate-setup guide.
fitboard: It walks you through five prompts about your place, your budget, the rooms, the style you like and the country, then assembles a furnishing plan drawn from real product listings, with actual store prices and photos rather than guesses. The total is capped at the budget you named, and it arrives as a PDF.
fashion-stylist: Photograph what you own and it builds a virtual closet from those images. From there it can cut try-on clips, put two outfits side by side, clean up a single garment into a reusable asset, and lay it out as catalog pages. It all lives in a style file you can reopen instead of starting over each season.
calendar-liftoff: Give it a theme, a subject or a year and it assembles a wall calendar as a print-ready PDF: twelve months, each with a full-bleed 4K photo chosen to fit the theme and a clean grid underneath. What arrives is a single file you can hand to a printer as-is.
photofix: Drop a folder of property shots and it edits the whole set in one pass, with the brightening and straightening listing photos need. Finished images return on a shareable drive for agents, photographers or rental hosts to hand to clients. Built by a drone crew that wanted less desk time.
presentation-coach: Takes a talk from idea to stage-ready: brainstorm the outline together, draft the slides and speaker notes, then run a rehearsal past it and get notes on the deck as well as your delivery. It works for in-person and remote talks of any size, and it never sits in on the live event or sends anything anywhere.
presentation-designer: Produces decks that already sit in your master template and house style, so the first slide is on-theme rather than blank. You describe the story, it builds the structure and styling, and hands back an editable link to keep refining in the tools your team already uses.
framecraft: An assembly seat inside Figma for product designers. It builds new frames and tidies existing ones with the library components already in the file, and it reads autolayout and spacing from the inspected properties rather than eyeballing them, so what comes back matches the file's own system.
wren-game-design-partner: A design partner for the phase before programming starts. It works a concept into a core loop and the hook that brings players back, then hands over a brief a developer or a coding agent can build from. When something exists, it reviews the result and returns a pass-or-fail verdict plus a ranked list of fixes.
mystery-eshopper: It walks an online store from landing page to checkout the way a shopper would, then grades the trip metric by metric, marking each one passed or failed with evidence attached. Problems come back as reproducible bug reports with screenshots or video. An owner gets an outside read on checkout without hiring a QA team.
data-viz: Paste a table or upload a CSV and it picks the form that truly fits the data, then makes the finding itself the headline. Already have a chart you half-distrust? Hand it over and it critiques it with a ranked list of fixes. It re-checks its own numbers, so the result holds up in a meeting.
rebrander: Owns a rename project from the day the decision lands. It searches the web for wherever the outgoing name still turns up, lays out a staged cutover plan and assembles a PDF report around it, generates a fresh logo kit to match, then keeps checking in until the last stray reference is gone.
gnome-stylist: Ask with words, a photo, or both together, and it returns exactly one picture — a gnome sporting the haircut you had in mind. The single-image rule keeps it fast and free of the infinite-variant rabbit hole, and the card is upfront that no humans are styled here. A small, odd, well-scoped bit of fun.
amazon-a-content-creator-kdp: A polish studio for the product pages behind self-published books. It plans the A+ module lineup, renders the artwork, and writes paste-ready copy that only says what the book and its blurb already claim. Everything lands staged for upload, and nothing goes live until you give the final go-ahead.
scroll-stitch: Send overlapping captures of the same scrolling page, or a recording of a vertical scroll, and it trims the status bars and browser chrome, aligns the overlap, and returns one seamless tall image. It works in English and Chinese, and says so plainly when the pieces will not join rather than forcing a bad seam.
mono-lisa: Runs a nightly product-design desk: when a metric falls off a cliff it investigates why, argues from first principles for what would fix it, then files the ticket with the chart included, and prepares three design options for a human gate before any of it reaches engineering. Mornings start with a case, not a mystery.
cross-border-money-desk: A client abroad paid you and the total arrived short — drop the invoice or the payout note here for a patient walkthrough: which transfer network carried the money, where fees nibble at it, and where the balance likely sits now. Educational by design — it explains payment flows and never touches funds or accounts.
ink: A pixel-art collaborator for game developers who start from generated imagery. Concepts become tidy, palette-consistent sprites and walk animations sized for real engines, exported in the formats an actual project needs. It covers the patient half of art production that polish usually waits on.
avatar-animator: Turns any image (a photo, pet, logo, or artwork) into a looping animated avatar with blinking eyes and moving backgrounds, and can set it as your bot's avatar. Runs free on your bot's own computer.
stevecad: A CAD design assistant that builds and edits 3D models, finds standard and off-the-shelf parts, and runs studies on your designs.
webi: A web designer and front-end coder that owns site look, mockups, art direction, and HTML/CSS/JS/WordPress code, and proves every live change on the real public URL.
clip-bot: Cuts social-ready podcast highlights from YouTube: captioned 16:9 clips with karaoke captions and a source card, then drops the file on your computer.
fuse: Watches your ad spend and performance and flags what's breaking before it burns budget. Works from a pasted export, and never pauses a campaign without your yes.
ai-search-visibility: Checks whether AI assistants and Google recommend you, and who they name instead. Starts from a handful of questions your buyers actually ask.
apple-search-ads-review: Reviews your Apple Search Ads spend against your cost per install target. Drafts the keyword, bid, and budget changes, and never touches your account.
event-producer: Turns your event details into a run of show, guest list, and day-of checklist. Tracks vendors, guests, dietary needs, and travel, and never sends a message without you.
human-copywriter: A human-voice rewrite desk for email, posts, blogs, DMs, landing-page bodies, and PR.
leadsworth: Scores your inbound leads, merges duplicates, assigns an owner, and flags what's stuck. Works from a CRM export, a sheet, or a paste, and never sends anything without you.
luma-pages: Builds and updates private Luma event pages for field marketers — copy, branding, registration settings, capacity and waitlist, and registration-list hygiene. Pairs with a Notion docs agent so the event brief and Luma page stay in sync.
tally: Turns your Google Ads, Meta, and LinkedIn exports into one weekly report with commentary. Answers reporting asks in Slack with real numbers, and never posts without your yes.
seo-aeo-desk: Turns your keywords into content ideas and writer-ready briefs for search and AI answers. Works from a pasted keyword list or your Search Console.
site-audit: SEO + content + speed + a11y + CRO + schema audit. Scored, P0/P1/P2, evidence URLs. Monthly diff. No invented metrics.
stills-clips-desk: Pulls stills, thumbnails, and short clips out of your footage, sized for where they go. Cleans up screenshots for docs too, and writes the caption and alt text.
best-video-editor: Turns uploaded footage into cut clips, burned-in captions, and platform-sized exports. Works from your notes and never overwrites the original.
writing-bot: A writing partner for drafting and revising essays, emails, docs, and other prose. It uses a structured revision workflow so the result is clearer and better organized while keeping the writer's meaning, facts, and voice.
wtd: WTD is a VIP hospitality planning partner for marketing ops — project-plan and status rhythm across tentpoles and ticket banks, nomination-sheet tracking, marketing-visible status hubs, and decks or agendas. Sales owns guest inviting; this bot keeps the plan and status clean without dumping private notes onto shared pages.
x-brief: On first chat, connect X, learn what you actually pay attention to from your recent posts, confirm that beat.
ratio: A second opinion before you hit send. Paste what you were about to publish and it picks out the sentence people will screenshot, explains what invites a pile-on, and offers a rewrite that keeps the argument you actually wanted to make. You are free to ignore all of it, and it has no way to publish anything itself.
desk-producer: A coordinator for creative production rather than a creative one. It fills the roles a working desk needs covered, keeps each piece of output filed as the day goes on, and closes every session with a packet of where things stood, so picking the project back up next week does not begin with an hour of hunting.
repost-x-posts: Mirrors new X posts to Threads, LinkedIn, Facebook, and Bluesky through Post Bridge. For people who post on X and want those originals everywhere.
adaptly-bot: Writes a post once, then queues and publishes it across nine networks on a timetable you set.
ads-operator: Builds ad plans for search and social, drafts budget shifts, and never touches your ad account without an explicit yes.
ai-video-expert: Turns one photograph and a line of direction into a brief clip with deliberate camera work rather than a drifting animation. Requires approval before anything goes public.
aoty-bot: Picks the week's 3 best new albums from Album of the Year scores and sends Apple Music links every Friday.
audiovisual-bot: Turns copy briefs into Instagram carousel and static art in a photo-on-top layout.
avatarmaker-bot: Generates and iterates avatar images for profiles and brands.
blair: Personal shopping agent that hunts used and secondhand designer goods across marketplaces, surfaces matches with pics and prices, and reaches out to sellers with your approval.
bookworm-bot: Handles the outreach side of an early launch: it writes invitations that sound like the founder rather than a mailing list, checks who has already been contacted so nobody gets the same note twice, and then sends them from your own address.
clipper: Takes footage from X or your own files, watches it, decides what the moment actually is, captions the talking GIFs.
cold-open-bot: It writes the script and waits for your approval before generating anything, which keeps a text-to-video tool from spending your budget on a premise you would have rejected.
content-growth-coach: Paste your YouTube, TikTok, X, or stream. It tells you what's holding the page back, what to fix first, and what to post next.
contentdrips-bot: Creates social media graphics and carousels in ContentDrips, then writes simple captions and schedules them to LinkedIn and Instagram.
contra-job-scraper-bot: Archives every listing to Notion and re-checks old leads, so the email you get is new openings and newly-closed leads rather than the same board reprinted four times a day.
dadprotech-brand-manager-bot: Studies how the account owner already writes on X, then proposes a single fresh post each weekday alongside a short list of conversations worth joining. Everything is a suggestion waiting on approval: it is a writing desk rather than an autoposter.
dan-patrick-bot: 1990s SportsCenter-style scores bot. Morning rundown plus a ping when your teams go final.
growth-desk: Draft-only X growth desk. You grow one named account. You do not research the feed. You do not post.
harry-dry-bot: A copy chief trained on Harry Dry. Rewrites landing pages, ads, emails, and share cards so every line is visual, falsifiable, and only you could say it.
icon-bot: Give it a subject and it renders a bust-up avatar in a consistent clay look: matte surfaces, soft lighting and tall dark oval eyes. It deliberately refuses flat vector marks and logos, so what comes back is a character rather than a brand asset. It works in Japanese.
ig-publisher-bot: Schedules and publishes Instagram carousels and posts from finished creative assets.
illo-bot: Close to zero setup: hand it the announcement or the post and it comes back with an illustration built around a mascot rather than a stock-looking image.
imogen-alt-text: Writes short alt text focused on the part of the image that actually matters, so posts stay accessible.
jester-bot: Hands meme-making over to a bot: describe the joke and it produces the picture or the short video version through the Memelord API, so you are not stitching a template together yourself. Useful when the reply is funnier as an image than as a paragraph.
keywire-bot: Would You Rather collector that gathers and organizes prompt-game content for KeyWire.
know-enemy-bot: You hand it the list of companies you want watched, and from then on it works strictly from material anyone could look up. Short briefings arrive at a regular beat with the movements worth knowing about, and in between you can call up a profile on any single rival the moment a deal or a launch makes it urgent.
likeness-bot: Locks a named person or animal from photos or a clip so later stills and clips keep looking like them.
lina-bot: YouTube studio director for creators. Designs one video at a time as a thumbnail–title–opening–payoff contract, then picks the next test.
paddy: YouTube strategist for creators who want the whole video judged, not just the title. Checks topic, title, thumbnail, spoken open, and what to leave alone after publish.
podcast-summary-bot: Summarizes podcasts and interviews from a YouTube, X, or Spotify link into five reusable insights plus deeper notes.
seo-geo-ads-shopify: A senior marketer for Google Ads, Meta, SEO, and Shopify. Connects the marketing stack to Grok in one click.
seo-geo-specialist-bot: SEO and GEO operator for people who want measurable rankings and AI citations. Uses Rankdelta.ai for research, rank tracking, technical audits, and AI visibility.
sharenow-feed-bot: Give it a topic and it tracks Instagram, X, Threads, YouTube and TikTok every hour onto a board that stays current. It needs a third-party ShareNow connection to publish.
short-form-scaler: Uses the Overlap AI API to find clips inside webinars, podcasts, and long-form videos — targeting at least four candidates per day for human pick.
shorty: Starts from proven performers rather than everything you have posted, picks the strong hooks, formats 9:16 with captions.
shotcraft: Builds a launch video from storyboard to sound mix: shot cards, live-page screenshots, and Remotion assembly with camera movement and timed cuts.
situation-monitor-bot: Follows the posts you bookmark on X across the week, then works out which of them actually amounted to something. At the end of the cycle it hands you a ready-to-edit thread covering those picks, matched to how you normally write so it needs little cleanup.
social-media-gtm-bot: Acts as a 24/7 Head of Content that plans multi-platform content calendars, recycles winning posts, builds lead magnets, and publishes via PlugKit.
socials-bot: Hourly X and Reddit scout that drops filmable AI and tech kits for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.
spotify-dj-bot: Controls Spotify: picks sets, suggests artists, and maps nicknames to devices.
trial-reels-bot: Pulls nine Reel candidates from one YouTube video and A/B tests versions against non-followers to find which idea deserves another iteration.
twitter-automations-bot: Three X automations for creators: DM people who comment a keyword, queue new followers above a size floor, and watch a locked list of accounts.
universal-video-downloader-bot: Paste a video link; get a playable MP4 from X, Reels, YouTube, TikTok, Vimeo, and 1500+ sites.
video-editor: Takes your raw footage and handles clips, cuts, sound, titles, pacing, and export — end-to-end video editing on its own machine.
vidmoat-bot: Cuts, previews, and renders videos in Vidmoat over MCP into an editable timeline.
walt-bot: Reviews a filmmaker agent's output against the brief you actually gave, calls keep or recut, and keeps the loop running rather than handing back the first render.
weekly-top-100-fans: Analyzes X API data to identify and rank your top 100 most engaged fans and followers each week.
x-account-crew-bot: Rather than one assistant juggling everything, the job is split five ways: someone digging up things worth posting about, someone sharpening the opening line, someone holding the calendar, someone reading what rival accounts are up to, and someone keeping an eye on your mentions.
x-algo: Reads the openly published For You ranking source alongside your recent post performance, then recommends whether to post fresh, quote, or wait.
x-high-coach: Drop an X username. Get a score, health flags, unfollow watch, and punchy rewrites for anyone who wants more reach and fewer surprises.
x-strategist-bot: Audience growth is treated here as a matter of relationships rather than volume. It follows who keeps turning up in your replies and quotes, tells you which of those accounts deserve your attention, and suggests how a throwaway exchange might be grown into something that lasts.
x-top-500-fans: Ranks your top 500 X fans each month by who liked your posts most.
tteok-i: X account editor. One diagnosis of what is holding the account back, one next post in their voice, plus the cut of what not to post.
connections-bot: Maps your X following and mutuals by location into a searchable Notion database you already own.
meme-king-bot: Makes still memes and GIFs from live X trends and news, plus a 3–5 meme morning drop. Never posts to X.
content-writer: Writes button labels, empty states, failure messages, hint text, and microcopy in plain English with one consistent voice.
music-video-release: Plans a music video from MP3, lyrics, and visual direction: brief, shot list, prompt board, stitch order, and release checklist.
kimi-obk8ft: Turns a podcast or YouTube episode into a concise cheat sheet with the core idea, practical steps, frameworks, warnings, and constraints.
x-account-strategist-pzshxl: Suggests X posts and articles for founders using relevant successful content and lessons from their own work.
myapps-video-desk-bot: Generates photoreal short video clips in a MyApps playground via input_text, then stitches the series into one final with local ffmpeg.
explainer-desk-bot: Explainer-video desk: drop a voice demo, PPT, optional avatar, and page-marked script; it schedules VO and a subtitle-aligned 1080p cut for talk clips and product intros.
video-transcriber-bot: Paste a YouTube, IG, TikTok, or X link — get a clean transcript (plain, SRT/VTT, speakers). Captions first; ASR only when needed.
arch-shorts-bot: Solo YouTube Shorts maker for architecture and civil-engineering explainers: script, Imagine cuts, dubbing, and mux — delivers the finished short.
klo-bot: TikTok creative strategy from 100 organic videos — sentiment, comments, video ideas.
clip-saver-bot: Cuts social-ready YouTube clips while offloading heavy work off the Grok Bot meter.
social-media-by-eclincher: It covers the working day of a social team end to end: queueing and sending posts out across more than a dozen networks, then gathering everything that comes back, from private messages to public reviews, into one place to be answered from. Live performance figures sit alongside the replies.
x-daily-posting-playbook: It sets up the machinery behind posting every day: a standing bank of subjects to draw from, a read on what is performing in your corner of the platform, drafts written to be pasted out as they are, sensible hours to send them, and a look back at what worked. Move accounts and it comes with you.
personal-brand-desk: It starts by looking back over your own posting history to see what actually earned attention, then puts forward five ideas with sources attached. Each one is written, picked apart and rewritten before it reaches you, and anything bound for LinkedIn sits on hold until you say the word.
blogdrafter: Drafts and edits blog posts that still sound like you wrote them.
ugc-bounty-manager: Handles the administration behind paying creators for clips and other audience-made content. It writes the instructions participants work from, goes through everything that comes back, and calculates what each accepted submission cost you per view. Amounts arrive as proposals for you to approve, never as transfers.
landing-page-generator: Aimed at one specific business rather than being a generic page builder. You hand over the product and what you charge for it; it drafts the persuasive copy, assembles the page and pushes it to a real URL. The prices shown are your actual prices, and the buy button is connected rather than decorative.
paid-ads-manager: Covers the whole advertising cycle instead of one slice of it: producing the creative, getting campaigns live, and checking on them every single day. Each morning it hands back a short summary of what happened overnight. Thresholds for killing a loser or putting more behind a winner are yours to set up front.
creator-shortlist-crew: Tell it the subject matter and the platform you care about and it goes hunting for the people posting there, then fills in how each of them can be reached. Fresh names keep arriving over time instead of all at once, so a partnerships team always has somebody new to approach this week.
serp-watch-team: Rankings are only half the picture now that people put their questions to a chatbot instead. This follows both sides: where your pages land on a results page, and whether assistants name you when the subject is your category. That becomes a regular digest with a view on what to write next.
linkedin-watch: Checks LinkedIn for you at set times rather than waiting for you to open the app. Each run gathers new activity across your feed, direct messages, connection requests, profile views and job matches, then posts a digest into chat with links to each item. If you prefer listening, it can read the cards aloud too.
aeo-content-producer: Takes readings of how often you surface inside AI-generated answers and turns them into an editorial plan: which existing pages need reworking, which subjects you have nothing on at all, then an outline and a draft for each. Everything is edited and then parked, waiting on your sign-off.
showrunner: The lead role in a five-part setup for making music videos. It settles the look, produces the reference frames, and spells out what every shot needs from Grok Imagine — feed those in yourself or let it render them — after which the finished clips are cut together against the track.
nugget-bot: Turns podcasts into social quote graphics and carousels — paste an episode, pick nuggets, drop a template ID.
owp-taste-bot: Taste seat for a small film/game huddle — grades stills, clips, and beds KEEP/HOLD/BIN; soft KEEP only when picture and on-ear both pass.
x-writer-bot: Learns any X account writing style, then drafts tweets, edits, and long-form posts in that voice.
project-manager: Marketing project manager that coordinates research, positioning, landing pages, ads, and analytics across specialist bots — with screenshot check-ins and human gates on merge and spend.
marketing-analyst: Google Ads–first performance analyst: turns exports into weekly and monthly reports with commentary, answers reporting asks with real numbers, and watches spend against your thresholds so you catch what's breaking before it burns budget. Never posts or touches a campaign without your yes.
performance-marketer: A performance marketer that turns Product Marketer ad copy into paused Maximize-clicks Google Ads Search shells for messaging tests — review sheets first, then traffic with live screenshots, no spend until you say so.
website-ops: Website operations and content manager. Ships site changes as PRs from your website repo, runs evidence-backed site audits (SEO, content, speed, a11y, CRO, schema), and turns Product Marketer briefs into landing-page PRs with in-chat screenshots.
product-marketer: Learns your product, brand, tone, and positioning principles; uses competitive research to sharpen how you stand out; drafts and crafts copy against those principles; and hands off landing-page and Ads copy to the rest of the marketing team.
market-researcher: Monitors your competitors' public websites, ads, marketing, pricing, and positioning on a standing cadence. Collects what changed, flags moves you should know about, and suggests concrete strategy adjustments or pivots. Never posts or contacts anyone.
marketing-bot-bragi: Turns any project into click-worthy X launch posts — single post, short thread, and reply bait from a simple brief.
wirey: Owns a daily AI hard-news briefing end to end: high-signal events, neutral wire script, ElevenLabs voiceover, edit dual-gate, and publish workflow.
drop-radar: Same-day DTC and beauty competitor product-drop watcher across Amazon, brand sites, and TikTok Shop — quiet on zeros, hits only.
media-manager-matt: Owns a YouTube channel's post-upload work: transcribe, captions, chapter timestamps, titles, descriptions, and thumbnails so you never open YouTube Studio by hand.
scribe-code: X livestream and replay note-taker: watches from a verified start, marks pivots and soft claims, delivers sanitized notes plus a paste-ready thread — draft-only, never posts.
fulcrum: Draft-only organic reply partner: surfaces ranked reply and thread opportunities with paste-ready drafts, optional daily briefs, and hard gates before anything public goes live.
press-code: Last-gate X publisher: QC on promo-confirmed copy, your final OK, then posts on X and proves it with the live URL — never skips brand or spend gates.
sharenow-bot: Builds clean static pages from your topic or content and publishes them to ShareNow.today, with optional hourly topic boards when you ask.
flip: Domain flip operator: takes parked domains, ships a narrow live offer fast, runs SEO and conversion until cash shows, and kills what does not print.
viral-analyst: Paste any X post you want to analyze into chat. Get a quick brief back on the hook or scroll stopper, why the content worked, the psychological patterns behind it, the structure and flow, the substance of the claims, and the reach potential. The best content creators study others.
gazetteer-scout: You name a niche. I find what that audience is beginning to need, check whether it is already answered, and write the missing piece only after KEEP.
five-stars: Keeps a small local business's Google, Facebook, Yelp, and TripAdvisor reviews answered. It drafts a reply to each new review in the owner's voice and flags urgent issues and complaint patterns, but never posts anything itself.
visibility-marketer: Free organic marketer for Grok Bot templates. Writes natural, human-feeling copy; finds no-new-account visibility; posts on accounts you already own when you grant access. No paid ads, no throwaway forums.
video-editor-2: Edits short vertical talking-head videos from your raw footage: picks the best takes, captions what you actually said, and adds B-roll, motion graphics, and music. Sends an edit plan for your yes before cutting, checks every cut for sync and glitches, and never posts.
distro-bot: Runs your marketing loop end to end: campaigns on your ad accounts, fresh creative, real channel analysis, timely posts from X and web scans, and outbound until a lead replies. Learns from your past campaigns and never changes spend, posts, or sends without your yes.
video-creator: Pick a topic and it runs the whole explainer pipeline for one video at a time: research, script, voice track, hand-drawn-style animation, edit, and a QA pass, ending with an unlisted YouTube upload for you to review. It spins up helper bots so several stages run side by side instead of in a queue.
children-s-book-chief-of-staff: A production partner for picture-book authors. Bring a manuscript for ages four to eight and it helps shape it into a beat sheet and a standard page layout, from the shorter seven-spread form to the classic thirty-two pages, then hands collaborators blank templates to work in. Structure and planning, not ghost-writing.
pearl: Built around one mission for your content: it turns that into a plan and delegates the pieces to specialist bots covering news gathering, drafting and graphics. Handoffs get reviewed rather than assumed, and anything outside the plan comes back to you first. The bot manages the work instead of doing it.
newsroom-to-teleprompter: You choose the beats and the voice, and it fills the rest: two researchers on the reading, an editor on the draft, and a fact-checker between the copy and publication, with a shared room tying the desks. It comes back built for the camera: a script paced for a teleprompter, plus the social posts to run with it.
archer: Runs a crew of specialists keeping an online product directory current, and spends its time managing rather than making. The day is shaped into five fixed briefs, each specialist is held to its own rules, and imagery is limited to pictures the operation actually has the licence to use.
cash-fleet-operator: Directs a small crew of specialists working an online catalogue: marketplace listings, printed merch and digital offers, plus the promotional posts pointing at them across platforms. The framing is ordinary e-commerce execution, each specialist kept in its own lane, every channel aimed at a real product page.
chief-of-staff-s4mu: Built around the reality of running a channel. It bundles YouTube-comment reports summarised in Italian and English and read through research, advisory and resolution angles, with a daily pass over an Outlook inbox for junk. Nothing is removed without asking, so the sweep stays reviewable.
x-free-credits-finder: It looks for posts that hand out credits for AI tools in exchange for a reply or a follow, then separates the ones worth your time from the dead and the doubtful. Each find comes with what the poster is asking for, so you know the price before you play. You can run the sweep on a schedule, up to twice a day.
paid-media: Keeps an eye on live channel and campaign performance as the numbers come in and proposes budget reallocations in Slack, always measured against your monthly cap. Nothing moves until you approve the suggestion, so the reallocation habit builds without anyone handing over the spending keys.
sanji: Paste a bio or a conversation and get a straight read on what is working. It tightens profiles, proposes stronger openers, and rewrites your draft reply two or three ways in different tones so you can pick the one that sounds like you. Feedback is blunt, no manipulation tactics, and you hit send yourself.
botman: A detective-themed guard for your social accounts. It reviews new followers and message requests, flags likely scams, bot accounts and impersonators, and writes a short case file for each suspect. It also summarizes publicly reported local crime activity, and carries a seasonal Halloween mode for parents.
product-ads: It starts from the photos and details you already have, building campaign drafts from them, then manages everything inside a fixed daily budget you set. Underperforming ads get paused and converting ones get scaled, following rules you agreed to in advance. Spend is reported from live numbers rather than estimates.
serp-specialist: Name a niche and a few towns and it maps real search volumes across those markets. It flags openings where the incumbent sites look beatable, grades a website's organic reach as well as how answer engines surface it, and puts together a demo site to pitch from. Research and drafting only, with no ranking promises.
event-guest-screener: Grades each event applicant against the customer profile you define, approving the strongest fits in bulk inside the invite tool itself, so the room ends up full of the right kind of attendee. The review that used to eat an afternoon before a launch becomes a short check of the edge cases.
optimusanesthesia: Writes the public-facing material a small practice needs: carousel posts, bio copy and patient explainers. Everything stays general information rather than guidance on an individual case, so the account stays firmly on the marketing side of that line. Suits a solo provider who posts irregularly.
cadence: It sits between you and the inbound: who may reach you is spelled out by person, channel and topic, and anything outside the list waits. Replies come back as drafts for you to send, a light contact record builds up, and automation runs only where you have allowed it. One desk for one owner's attention.
youtube-title-description-writer: Paste in the transcript of a video you have made and it comes back with three title candidates, a description worth publishing, and chapter marks whose timestamps line up with the transcript. Every suggestion is staged for review, so nothing reaches an upload until you have signed off on the wording.
tape-bot: It follows the podcasts and YouTube shows you subscribe to and republishes a tidied copy just for you: ad segments sliced out, your own chapter markers added, original notes and artwork kept intact. Everything lands on a private RSS address any player can take.
smudge: Hand it a draft with that obvious machine polish and it rewrites the phrasing until it reads like something a person typed. It does not hide its work: every tell it removed and every pattern it changed is listed, so you can review the edits and keep only the ones you agree with.
scotty: A product strategist aimed at independent makers and lean crews that cannot afford a planning department. It weighs the options and commits to what should ship next, then turns that decision into briefs you can paste straight into whatever build tool you are using, so planning and doing stay connected.
quill: A craft pass for writing in an Obsidian vault. Pick one mode per run: punch up the voice of a draft, check that a new note stays consistent with the rest of the graph, or take a depth read that pushes a thin note further. It patches what you point at instead of rewriting wholesale, and it never invents canon.
bookmark-miner: Everyone saves posts they never revisit. This one reads through the bookmarks on your own X account via the connector and returns a short, ranked punch list: skills worth writing up, projects worth starting, and features worth adding to something you already build.
xchat: On a repeating cycle it searches X for new ways people are using Grok bots, keeping only posts that include a template or a step-by-step how-to and skipping the hype. Each pick is summarized, translated and posted into an XChat group you run, so members get usable material instead of a firehose.
scroll: It reads your Following timeline in chronological order, deliberately skipping the algorithmic feed, and sends a short weekday rundown of the posts worth your attention: who wrote each, why it matters, and the link. An hour of scrolling becomes a two-minute read. Read-only, and it never engages for you.
gif-bot: Describe a YouTube moment and it finds that exact stretch, burns the spoken lines onto the frames as captions, and exports a muted clip sized for phones. You get GIF and MP4 versions that drop straight into a group chat. Nothing is posted anywhere; the files are yours to share.
open-call-producer: Paste in an exhibition open call and it breaks the brief into what selectors actually want - theme, sizing, file specs, deadlines. It benchmarks your images against those requirements, flags the gaps, and assembles a package with every spec verified. You review and send it yourself: nothing is submitted for you.
personal-site-builder: Turns a short description of yourself into a scaffolded personal website, works through the domain headaches that usually stall the project, and leaves you a live starting point to refine. The blank-page problem is gone before you have opened an editor.
community-operations-manager: Keeps an ambassador scheme moving: applications are reviewed, inbound DMs across the various channels get sorted, and cadence-based nurture is drafted so the community no longer needs a full-time person. The humans spend their time on members who need a person, not on sorting the queue.
merch-fulfillment-operator: Handles the swag pipeline from first message to dispatch: prospect outreach goes out, the redemption form is watched, each approve-or-reject call arrives as a chat ping, and the box ships once you sign off. Sending merch to the right people stops being a spreadsheet and a pile of screenshots.
newsletter-writer: Puts together each month's newsletter out of the launches, wins and calendar highlights worth sharing, written the way you write, then leaves it parked as a draft so the final edit and the send remain yours. The recurring excuse that there was nothing to say stops working, because the material is already gathered.
content-calendar: Acts as the scheduling brain for content spread over several channels: it hands out posting slots, lines up multi-day arcs, untangles clashes, and holds the line at a single daily post on each channel using your timezone. Writing and publishing stay with the other desks; this one only decides when things go out.
independent-author-hub: Coordinates the behind-the-scenes work of a self-published author: keeping the website current, moving the newsletter pipeline along, holding the promo calendar and clearing mailing-list chores in one place. Nothing is published, no DNS is touched and no money is spent until the author approves each step.
ride-editor: Housekeeping for a driving-footage channel: titles get rewritten to be searchable, playlists get a sensible order, and the raw miles get cut into highlight reels with thumbnails to match. Nothing publishes by itself - finished work sits staged until you approve it, so the backlog shrinks while the channel stays yours.
x-hygiene: Reviews the accounts that follow you and the ones you follow back, and tells you the price of the cleanup before any of it happens. You get a ranked set of block and unfollow suggestions, each with a link straight to the profile, inside limits you choose per run, per month or per week. It acts on nothing itself.
x-agent: Follows the AI and developer conversations where a reply from you would be worth reading, and drafts those replies so they sound like you. Every one of them waits at an approval step, and nothing is posted until you pass it, which means staying active without giving up control of the account.
xx-engineeringarteditor-xx: Treats a technical sketch as a piece bound for readers rather than one ticket among many, taking a rough engineering drawing and refining it until it holds up on a printed page. Each job is handled on its own terms, with care split between whether the drawing is right and how the finished page looks.
podcast-pipeline: Covers the whole production line for an audio programme: it researches the topic, writes a script with a distinct voice for each host, stitches the speech with your branding and an outro, checks the result, then cuts captions and publishes. Built around a beginner-level Spanish show, it handles two-host formats.
fernando-arana: Acts as your stand-in on WhatsApp by opening the desktop web client and working through unread conversations. For each thread it proposes a reply in your usual tone and holds it for your approval, so nothing leaves until you confirm it. Useful when you are away from the phone but still want messages answered promptly.
skool-community-bot: Sits alongside a Skool group you administer, working through an ordinary browser session instead of an official connector. It sums up who has joined and what has been posted, drafts follow-up messages for you to look over, and gathers the questions still without an answer into a list you can work through.
curious-first-time-reader: Give it a public page, an essay, or a playable demo and it reads the way a stranger would, knowing nothing about the project beforehand. It reports the exact spots where a newcomer stalls: jargon that went unexplained, assumptions you forgot you made, and the point where they would have quit. Run it before you ship.
lighting-specialist: Works like a senior lighting designer brought in on a production or a building fit-out. It picks fixtures, runs the photometric numbers, lays out DMX, sACN or Art-Net control, and draws the plot. The written spec it hands over is meant to survive a contractor or an inspector reading it, not just look tidy in a chat.
game-builder: Produces small games that genuinely run and open with no connection needed. There is a real way to win and a real way to lose, optional scorekeeping, and placeholder data throughout so something is playable before real numbers exist. Credits are spent only on what you actually requested.
yusician: Produces a complete track from a style note and a set of words, running the music model on your own Apple-silicon hardware instead of in somebody else's cloud, and returning a high-sample-rate audio file. The weights carry a non-commercial licence, so what you make is for personal projects rather than paid work.
realitycheck: Give it a handle and it returns an authenticity read: a number, a color meter, and the strongest warning and green markers taken from what the profile shows publicly. It is framed as an estimate rather than a verdict — a quick way to weigh whether that new follower is a person or part of a follow farm.
x-scout: A research assistant for X that stays on the reading side only: it maps who talks to whom inside a circle and how a topic develops over time. It never publishes, likes, follows or messages anyone, so the account it watches is never touched. Setup means your own SocialData key plus a spend limit agreed on the first run.
follows: It reads your X follower list and reports the movement: who arrived, who left, and which of the people you follow now follow you back, with a longer recap at the end of each week. An optional loop can return a follow, but only for accounts you have approved one by one. Nothing else on your account is touched.
lookalikes: A watchdog for your own username. On a schedule it sweeps the platform inside a topic lane you choose, then flags freshly created profiles that resemble yours closely enough to confuse people. It only reports what it finds, and it never posts, replies or follows anyone on your behalf.
creative-opps-oracle: A talent-scout desk for a single working independent artist. It starts by auditing your public presence so it knows how you actually work, then rounds up what is currently open — calls for work, grants, residencies and paid gigs — across art, music, code, games, film and writing. One artist at a time.
crosscheck: Before a page or pitch goes out, every load-bearing claim is walked past two separate reviewers: one argues the reasoning, the other chases live sources. Each claim returns graded as backed, shaky, contradicted or unverifiable, with suggested repairs for the ones that fail.
creator-tracker: Pick the accounts worth watching and it pings you the moment they post, with the link and a one-sentence digest of what changed. Alerts can be narrowed to a single topic you name, and a daily leaderboard shows which of your picks actually produced.
x-follower-spam-scanner: A quality check for your audience. It scans your followers for spam accounts, obvious bots, hollow parody or fan accounts, and impersonators, then reports what it found and waits: every block is confirmed with you before it happens. Useful after a viral moment, when the follower count jumps and not all of it is people.
ho-be-gone: Keeps watch on your follower list and on who has been interacting with you, then blocks the ones that read as scams, copycats or bot accounts. Every block feeds the filter, so the corrections you make afterwards shape what gets blocked the next time around.
seo-expert: Point it at a product website and it tracks how that site performs in search, watching the numbers over time instead of grading once.
