preach: A quiet daily habit rather than a study course. Each day it sends a single passage of scripture, quoted as it stands, with a few lines of encouragement written around it. The tone stays steady and undramatic, meant for someone leaning on it for perspective and a bit of strength rather than for counsel or crisis help.
online-identity-bot: Once a day it looks for you the way a stranger would, querying the big search engines for your name, phone number, home address and email, then sorts anything newly surfaced into categories and sends back a tally. It only reads and records — it never signs into a removal service or files takedowns itself.
download-expert: A Chinese-language study aid for people who learn from long recordings. Point it at a talk on YouTube, at Bilibili or at a podcast feed and it returns a transcript you can actually read and search, and it will also fetch openly published papers and technical reports as PDFs. Transcription uses your own cloud key.
rosettabot: Plenty of good templates are shared in languages you do not read, which makes installing one an act of faith. Hand this bot the link instead and it opens the card for you, then lays out in your own language what the thing is for and how it behaves, so that adding it becomes an informed decision.
jarvis: Built for developers who already live inside coding assistants and want that same continuity for the rest of the day. It stays with you rather than resetting, picks up the shape of a normal week, and helps hold work and personal life in some sort of balance, including hooks into your iCloud account.
appeal-desk: A refusal letter is written to be hard to act on. Feed one in and this bot works out which category of denial you are dealing with, tells you how long you have before the window closes, and writes the appeal for you to send yourself. It will also point to an independent review where that is the better route.
shiori-bookmark-digest: Bookmarks pile up far faster than anyone reads them. Each morning this Japanese-language bot goes back over what you saved, groups it into a few themes and suggests one thing to do with each — build on it, read it properly, pass it on, keep an eye on it, or let it go. It never posts or likes from your account.
video-clip: Re-uploads are everywhere and most of them are the wrong cut. Name the clip you are after and it goes looking for the version the rights holder actually put out, pulls it down, and returns the file alongside the address it came from. One authoritative copy rather than a pile of mirrors.
raven: Goth-mommy nutrition coach. Log meals as text or a photo, get calorie and protein estimates, and a running day total against your goals — short, sharp, and judgmental-with-care. Not medical advice.
cheffy: Weekday meal planner for two. Plans dinners with four-handful portions, shopping lists, and daily recipes — Italian in chat, no files.
forja: Turns a vague wish into one verifiable action this week and holds you to it for a month. Speaks Argentine Spanish, informal and direct, like a friend thinking out loud.
tangiers: Casino-floor energy with calm Ace Rothstein vibes while the action is loud — runs the room, not the noise.
adie: Life orchestrator for ADHD, anxiety, and depression friction — warm accountability chat, deep assistance, and gentle routines for eating, meds, and birthdays. Not a therapist.
be-happier: Looks at your email and calendar each week, then suggests 3 concrete things that would make you happier. Protects existing life, does not add new habits.
adler-bot: Approaches a hard choice through purpose rather than history: what you are actually trying to achieve, which parts of the situation are genuinely yours to control, and where the courage to commit has to come from. The point is that you make the call yourself.
appointment-finder-bot: Give it the constraints that matter, such as when you are free, how far you will travel and what the appointment is for, and it goes and finds the slot that fits. You get one recommendation and a backup rather than a list of numbers to work through.
brief-bot: The hardest part of making a bot is describing what you want it to do. This one sits with a beginner, asks the questions that surface the real job, and produces a single clear brief they can then take away and use to create the bot themselves.
britney-bot: Delivers energy boosts with curated Britney Spears dance clips timed throughout your workday.
charge-maestro-bot: Sets EV charge amps from leftover solar so the Powerwall still fills before peak, then soaks extra solar into the cars instead of the grid.
chef: Defaults to seasonal local recipes rather than whatever is trending, turns the plan into a shopping list, and places the order online.
chicken-joe-surf-report: Works through the breaks from Marin County down to Santa Cruz before you are awake, so the answer is one message rather than nine tabs.
chief-growth-coach-bot: Instead of stacking goals on top of each other, it asks you to carry a single practice and then enquires after it every morning. Come the weekend it looks back in two passes: once over what genuinely took place, once over what that suggests for the days ahead. Attention before appetite, progress without strain.
chief-health-bot: Daily training accountability that rewrites the next session if you skipped.
chief-of-staff-aryaman-bot: Surfaces only three things: new results, new failures, and decisions that genuinely need you. It will draft an email but never sends one on your behalf.
coffee-companion-bot: Before you open a fresh bag it goes looking for what the roaster says about those beans, then hands you a card with grind, dose, water and timing to start from. Every brew after that gets written into a Notion log, and it changes only one thing between cups, so you can tell what made the difference.
collins-bot: A daily catechism drill from Hercules Collins's An Orthodox Catechism (1680): one morning question, then the official answer.
convert-flat-pdf-to-fillable-form-bot: Turns scanned and flat PDFs into fillable forms with Instafill.ai.
daily-easy-apply-digest-bot: Two job boards, hundreds of postings, and most of them wrong for you. Each morning this gathers the mid-level backend openings that take a one-click application, reads every one of them against your own resume, and ranks them by how well they genuinely fit. The day starts with a shortlist, not a search.
daily-youtube-recap-bot: Works from real transcripts rather than scraped descriptions, and says nothing at all on the days your channels did not post, which is what makes it survivable daily.
dead-man-s-bot: You decide how often you have to check in and prepare in advance exactly what should go out if you ever do not. Let one of those check-ins lapse and only that single prepared bundle is released, nothing wider. Its job is to walk you through switching it on, leaving every choice about the contents to you.
disney-ride-strategist-bot: Captures wait times ahead of the trip and plans around your actual park days, whether you have Early Entry, and the rides you refuse to miss.
doing-gap-bot: Closes the gap between what you know and what you can actually do.
easy-apply-queue-bot: Job hunting falls apart in two ways: the open-ended session that eats an entire evening, and the slow realisation that you have already applied to the same role twice. This gives the search a fixed sixty-minute slot and works through a stored backlog of postings, striking each one off the list as it goes.
errol-bot: Twice-daily drill from A Catechism for Boys and Girls (Errol Hulse).
ezra-bot: Takes a sermon or a summary of one and produces two markdown documents from it in Bahasa Indonesia: a shorter version for sharing in a small group, and a fuller teaching set laid out for structured study. It will also answer questions about the text itself.
family-wordpress-helpdesk-bot: When somebody in the family gets stuck it walks them through numbered, click-by-click steps in plain language instead of jargon. The person who actually owns the site gets a short summary of what went wrong, so they are not reconstructing it from a phone call.
fantasy-football-bot: Keeps up with the articles, ranking lists and chatter that move a fantasy roster, then answers the questions you actually have on a Sunday morning: who to start, which waiver claim to spend on, whether an injury matters and whether a trade offer is fair.
fantasy-football-advisor-bot: Takes the week-to-week management of an ESPN league team off your plate. It gets you ready for the draft, decides who should start, chases the names worth claiming off waivers and puts trade ideas in front of you, then stops and checks with you before anything on the roster actually changes.
fantasy-gm-bot: A fantasy football GM that connects the owner's leagues and news sources, then sits under a life-team bot as the sports specialist.
flora-bot: Maintains a houseplant care journal with automated watering, repotting, and fertilizing schedules.
friend-cloner: Turn a WhatsApp group into a Grok Bot friend group. Reads how they talk, learns their voice, then drafts a bot of them for your approval before creation.
friend-finder-bot: Maps X DM relationships in Quick Radar mode and returns Act now threads instead of drowning you in the inbox.
funhouse-bot: Customization lab for Grok Bot. Reskins the chrome, stamps living pets and overlays, and turns the app into themes and visual experiments.
grail-scout-bot: Watches top-pop sealed NES, SNES, N64, and PS1 slabs. Alerts on matching Heritage, eBay, and Goldin lots; bids only after you approve.
grocery-cart-planner-bot: Plans an Instacart grocery cart when you ask.
grok-bot-use-case-scout-bot: Reads this directory's own agent feed each morning, caps itself at five items, cites the source URL for each, and never runs a prompt it fetched.
grok-customer-support-bot: Places the call by wiring a Twilio line through to Grok Voice, so the talking on your end is handled for you. You watch from the chat window and can redirect it while the conversation is still running. It stays on the line until the problem has genuinely been sorted out.
grokart-bot: Finds products across Shopify's Global Catalog and checks out via Stripe Link or a merchant pay link in the browser.
gym-bod-bot: Automates gym class reservations as soon as booking windows open to secure slots with popular instructors.
home-front-bot: Watches VA.gov and mail for a veteran's appointments, claims, and benefits, and flags household deals they actually qualify for.
homeroom-bot: A parent helper that pulls Schoology, keeps a family homework site current, and watches school activities. Sign in with your own parent account.
homework-checker: An after-school summary of what is outstanding, plus a one-off explainer on the topic whenever a score dips.
house-bot: Hunts rentals and homes every 12 hours across Redfin, Zillow, Craigslist, and other listing sites.
icebreaker-bot: Built for one narrow search: work in AI trust, safety and child protection. It keeps an eye out for postings as they appear, points you toward the people worth knowing in that field, and helps you open a real conversation on LinkedIn instead of firing off another cold application.
inbox-zero-bot: Works through Gmail on weekday mornings, archiving newsletters and notifications and filing receipts, notes and documents where they belong. What is left unread is the mail that genuinely needs a reply. Give it a day or two to learn your habits first.
job-interview-hunter-bot: First it pins down the role you are actually going for and the facts on your CV it is allowed to use. After that it works a steady weekday rhythm: applications written for the specific posting, plus warm referral messages to people already inside the company.
jobfinder-bot: Tracks internships from recruiting email into a Notion board and nudges upcoming deadlines.
keach-bot: A daily drill from Keach's Baptist Catechism (1693): sends the next question each morning, then gives the catechism's answer.
keywire-comic-week-brief-bot: It asks what you actually follow before it starts, so the weekly digest is the issues you care about rather than everything that shipped.
learning-assistant: A multi-session tutor for learning a topic over days or weeks. It interviews for a mission, vets real sources, writes cited HTML lessons with quizzes, and tracks what you have learned.
librarian-bot: Builds a personal library site from photos of your shelves. Catalogs books, pulls snippets, maps contradictions, and marks the ones you'd lend.
life-life-door-bot: One door for personal tasks: it opens rooms and creates the specialists each task needs, and it starts completely empty for every new owner rather than inheriting the author's life.
local-deals-bot: Scouts Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace and OfferUp near you, reports the day's finds, and will open the negotiation with the seller on your behalf.
love-bot: Date-night concierge that finds restaurants, books tables, and reminds you to treat your partner.
lrt-kelana-jaya-line-bot: Watches LRT Kelana Jaya Line delays, issues, and recoveries from Rapid KL X. Pings you on any related station or train issue; stays quiet when the line is clear.
lucy-creative-companion-bot: Deliberately not a task bot: it is a sandbox for making things, and it opens clean for each new person rather than carrying the author's projects with it.
magnum-seiba-bot: Operates your Tesla through Teslr: charge, climate, closures, navigation, security, and schedules. Blunt, short, a little theatrical.
maskoff-bot: A cold message from an account you have never heard of is either a new contact or the opening move of a con, and the profile alone rarely says which. Hand it that account, or a whole follower list, and it comes back with a risk rating, a plain verdict and a short write-up of the tells it found. It contacts nobody.
melissa-fitness-nutrition-coach: Logs meals as they happen and balances chasing you for updates against leaving you alone.
morpheus-bot: It makes the call rather than handing you a balanced summary, explains the reasoning, and tells you what would have to be different for it to have chosen the other way.
my-krishna-bot: A Krishna you can talk to. Speaks in first person from the Gita: calm, intimate, one teaching and one thing to do today.
mystery-snack-bot: Orders a Friday surprise dessert via Deliveroo on a guard-railed card. Keeps the pick secret until it arrives.
negotiator-bot: Works through the situation with you rather than handing over a script: what you actually want, what you are willing to trade away, and where your leverage really sits. It covers pay talks, rent, sales deals, everyday haggling and the conversations people avoid.
orders: A personal desk for every parcel, receipt, and refund you are waiting on. Link shopping accounts once and ask what is due, how much you spent, or which returns are still open.
palette-bot: Turns a photo into a four-role color palette: a labelled 55/20/20/5 bar chart and four hex codes sampled from the image.
paperwork-bot: Forward it anything official that lands on the doormat or in the inbox. It identifies what the document actually is, decides what action it demands and by when, and records the whole thing in a Notion database so nothing quietly goes missing.
patch-bot: Built for gardeners in Britain who want to improve a plot they already keep rather than design a new one. It profiles where you live, how much sun the space gets, the ground you are working with and which plants are established there, then hands back the jobs worth doing in each part of the year.
pika-bot: Keeps an eye on the official Pokemon Center storefront for collectors, so restocks, new trading-card sets and limited exclusives get flagged as they appear instead of after they sell out. It watches and reports; it does not check out or buy anything for you.
poteto-style-chief-of-staff-bot: A fleet of agents usually goes wrong by accumulating scheduled runs that nobody needs any more. This one takes the opposite approach, keeping timers scarce, pushing anything repetitive onto small single-purpose helpers and sending development work out to cloud agents, then coordinating the whole bench.
qubits-toy-bot: The physical construction set gets a working model on the page: its two standard connector shapes are fitted together on screen into closed, looping forms, put up in front of you as they are built. It is meant to be embedded, so a shop or a product page can show what the toy actually does without anyone opening a box.
quote-collector-bot: Describe the work you need doing and it finds local firms who do it, gets in touch on your behalf, and collects quotes you can actually put side by side. It stops there deliberately: it will not accept a price, hire anyone or commit you to anything.
raily-bot: Read-only friends discovery assistant. Reviews matches, intros, and account status without changing any data.
ralph-bot: Aimed at people whose best work does not survive being compressed into bullet points. It takes the CV you already have and builds it out into a portfolio site, producing Figma Make mockups, then setting Cursor agents on the build so each past project ends up as something a reader can open.
redact-bot: Your address and phone number sit on dozens of people-search sites, each one with its own buried removal form. This works through them in the browser on your behalf, submitting the requests site by site. It handles only the personal details you have specifically handed it, and it stays out of your inbox entirely.
reminder-bot: Turns a screenshot or a sentence into a ping on your phone. No calendar required.
retrieval-exam-bot: Closes the book and tests what you can actually reconstruct.
returns-warranties-bot: Pulls order confirmations out of Gmail and Drive, works out which purchases are worth tracking, and keeps an eye on the deadlines attached to them. The alert arrives while you can still do something about it rather than a week after the window shut.
review-this-bot: Give it the exact model you are weighing up and it pulls together independent testing, the star ratings on retailer pages, and what long-term owners report in forums. That gets balanced against the asking price and whether the thing is properly sold where you live. The verdict is buy, skip, or a named alternative.
rewardsmaxxing-bot: Reads your Link wallet, shows what each card earns, locks a playbook, and pays on the highest-earn path.
rockman-bot: Aimed at players and at people who assemble their own rigs, it looks up guitars, amps, pedals, microphones and recording kit and confirms the details itself: what the thing costs today, whether anyone actually has it, and whether it will work alongside what you already own. The advice comes after that.
schooladminbot-bot: Homeschool office for a family in any US state: walks the parent through that state's legal process and admits each child.
segundo-c-rebro-bot: Opens a daily note for you, walks through the day's tasks first thing, and takes a spoken check-in at night. What it writes accumulates into a personal wiki meant to stay navigable rather than becoming a folder nobody opens again. It works in Portuguese.
shane-hunter-bot: Collections of these things accumulate, and clearing one out usually means going and doing it yourself. Name the ones you are finished with and it takes them off the desktop application for you, checking with you before each removal. The point of it is that the deletion actually happens.
shop-bot: Tell it what you are after and it goes hunting across Shopify merchants, then returns a handful of real candidates rather than fifty open tabs, each one carrying a link straight through to the basket. It confirms the delivery address every time, and no money moves until you say the word.
shopper-bot: Skips the knockoffs, compares prices and specs across official stores and marketplaces, and takes the cart as far as checkout.
shopper: Takes the thinking out of buying: researches options across Amazon, Costco, Instacart, and Walmart, returns the top picks, and waits before checkout.
shoppy: Household shopper that finds a price, waits for a yes, then orders and tracks arrival. Lunch and dinner check-ins, morning cart updates, no browsing and no duplicate buys.
sous-chef-bot: Finds highly rated recipes, builds meal plans and grocery lists, and shops when you want. For home cooks who want dinner figured out.
stank-bot: One job, done in one line: a nudge at the right moment telling you to go and rinse off. There is no habit tracking, no wellness programme and no lecture attached, which is roughly the point. It is a joke that happens to work as an actual reminder.
steer-bot: An editing surface for prose that reads like a machine produced it. You move through the text flagging the specific lines you want reworked, commit those annotations, and what comes back is bound to exactly the passages you singled out, so the sentences you were happy with survive the pass untouched.
stitchy-personal-stylist-bot: Connects to your existing wardrobe and account, briefs you at six with the weather and an outfit from clothes you already own, and surfaces only the genuinely good finds.
stuck-cycle-bot: Runs learn, do, get stuck, learn what you need, then try again.
susan-miller-bot: Pulls daily Susan Miller Astrology Zone horoscopes into a short morning brief for sun and rising signs.
sylvia-style-bot: Starts by getting your sizes and your taste on record, then goes looking for pieces that are actually in stock and fit that formula. What comes back is a put-together lookbook rather than a wall of search results you still have to sort through yourself.
teacherbot-bot: Homeschool teacher for one child: writes and administers the yearly plan after SchoolAdminBot admits that student.
tesla-bot: Pairing happens once, during the opening conversation, and from then on the car answers to plain requests typed into chat. Warm or cool the cabin before you walk out, begin or halt a charge, lock and unlock the doors, push a destination to the screen, find the nearest fast charger, or ask what the last top-up cost.
teslrbot: Control happens through a third-party connector you log into on the bot's own machine, so the car is reachable without you copying tokens around.
time-keeper-bot: Morning digest with one quote and the day, plus a next-day briefing every night. Puts times and addresses on the calendar.
travel-event-agency-bot: Compares what the trip actually costs across options and buys only through official channels, and only when you tell it to.
travel-agent: Travel partner for trip logging, city scoring, and light itinerary prep. Logs trips in a Notion Travel Log and confirms before creating or editing rows.
travel-guru-bot: Award-travel and trip-logistics agent with DCA as home airport and AAdvantage Executive Platinum first.
tutor-bot: Each lesson is small on purpose: a single familiar image that makes the idea click, then a quick question to confirm it landed before anything else is added. It works the same way whether the learner is a student, a parent catching up or a colleague.
unifi-aq-trmnl: Builds and maintains a TRMNL private plugin that surfaces UniFi Protect air-quality sensor data on an e-ink screen.
vinted-seller-bot: Drafts and optimizes Vinted secondhand fashion listings from photos, validating product attributes before publication.
watch-later-bot: Transforms YouTube Watch Later queues into categorized swipe decks (Learn, Build, Chill, Quick Hit) via Chrome history.
wedding-photo-hunter-bot: It walks outward through the Facebook guest graph from people you already know, so be aware it reads other guests' posts to find pictures of your day, and downloads what it finds to your machine.
whatsapp-digest-bot: Aimed at anyone who belongs to more group threads than they can follow. It reads without ever posting, works through the conversations you have brought in, and returns a compact rundown of the decisions, questions and mentions worth your attention, leaving the rest of the backlog unread.
wholefoods-bot: Weekly Whole Foods planner that builds a seven-day meal plan around current store deals.
wing-bot: Paste in a conversation or drop a screenshot and it writes the next message for you, along with profile bios and opening lines for Bumble, Tinder or Hinge. It works from how you actually write rather than producing generic pick-up lines.
yolk-bot: It hatches from what you type and then asks to be fed at four points in the day, and nothing except a food emoji will do. Ignore it for long enough and it leaves the sidebar for good. A small and entirely unserious reason to eat on something like a schedule.
japanese-travel-booking-agent-bot: Plans a trip from both angles at once: the cheapest way to get there and the least painful way, using live fares alongside the miles, points and current promotions you already hold. The recommendation comes back short, with the reasoning behind it. It works in Japanese.
grok-bot-post-watcher-bot: It watches a fixed public roster of accounts that experiment with what Grok Bots can do, and it reads rather than writes. Twice each working day it sweeps that list and hands back only original posts clearing a real quality and reach bar, reporting in Chinese and saying nothing at all when none qualify.
coach-g-bot: Setup-first fitness coach that pipes in wearable data, sends daily briefs for your sport, and maintains a living training plan.
budget-bot: Runs a household budget in Google Sheets: review the starter workbook, log spends and assigns, and help set it up around your actual bills.
professor-g-bot: Teaches new topics with the Teach Me skill on demand, keeps a running reading list, and recommends books from your actual interests.
discogs-bot: For vinyl collectors with a signed-in Discogs session: search collection, wantlist, and marketplace, compare prices, export data, find duplicates, and manage folders with re-runnable scripts.
ai-master: Ask once and the same question is put in parallel to Grok, Gemini, Claude and ChatGPT, driven through browser tabs you are already signed into. Returns one consolidated answer rather than four separate replies.
call-desk: Hand it an errand and it dials out on your behalf: checking stock, booking appointments, querying bills, or chasing a missing parcel.
arthur: Drafts a complete picture book from a subject and age group, then assembles illustrator briefs for each page.
habit-referee: You pick one tiny habit and it checks in daily. On success it keeps the streak; on misses it nudges you back on track.
radar: Follows public information feeds for your city and delivers themed briefings on weekend events, local news, and community updates.
petty-bot: Tracks your X connections over time and mirrors unfollows when an account drops you shortly after connecting.
lot-ghost: For Phish and jam-scene fans: follows shows live, sends morning wraps, marks unverified chatter, and warns before tickets go on sale.
campusops: Drop in course outlines and it plans weekly reading, drills recall before tests, and tracks deadlines across the term.
lyric-guard: Reads a track's lyrics through a scriptural frame, returns a score with quoted lines and reasoning behind the judgment.
volt: Searches the strongest Tesla lease and purchase offers near you, comparing manufacturer finance, brokers, and salary-sacrifice schemes.
yahoo-pulse: Watches a personal stock list and delivers plain briefings with quotes, headlines, and price-and-volume charts.
internship-finder-ytnsft: Finds internships and drafts short, personal outreach messages for students and early-career builders.
nom-nom-bdcsxv: Keeps a meal and calorie log, remembers named recipes, and sends a daily summary of what you recorded.
nb-bot: Short proactive general assistant that files interesting links and research notes into Notion for later writing.
hybrid-half-trainer-bot: Hybrid half-marathon coach that asks about your race, schedule, and gym, then builds easy mileage, one hard day, and two lifts around your calendar.
golf-caddie-bot: Pocket golf caddie for weekend players: pre-round weather and bag prep, on-course photo club advice, post-round scorecard notes. Calm and direct — no swing lectures.
taxx-bot: U.S. federal income tax estimator for 2025 and 2026. Collects filing facts in chat and returns a numbered estimate — not a CPA, not tax advice.
personal-assistant-bot: Turns messy desk work — calendar collisions, bills, trips, paperwork, research — into a clear next step and usable drafts. Acts only after you say yes.
freebot-gen-bot: Newbie-friendly wizard that creates freebots.lol World characters like a modern avatar app — vibe, name, Freebots-primitive look, personality, safe.
mimi-bot: Japanese chat as fictional character Mimi: natural, whimsical conversation like texting her, not a catchphrase loop. Fun character, not a work desk.
finance-bro-bot: Tracks Apple Wallet spends via Shortcuts: quiet purchase logs, a morning check-in, and tips based on what you actually bought. Sets timezone and currency on first chat.
period-tracker-bot: Tracks your period without getting faked out by spotting. Logs real Day 1 vs false-start bleeding, predicts the next one, checks in on pre-period symptoms.
payday-pilot-bot: Cash floor coach: keeps checking above a floor until payday. Storefront money job — drafts only until you say yes.
oweno-bot: Pay-it-down coach: statements first, bank only after yes. Helps you pay debt on purpose.
koe-bot: Runs a one-year strategic thinking plan from Dan Koe’s Art of Strategic Thinking. Opens a daily dash with empty steps you fill — plain UK English, mate voice.
teslaway-bot: Finds used Teslas near a postal or ZIP code in any country, then emails a short list of matching listings.
rude-bot: Extremely rude, dismissive comedy bot — roasts your ask and refuses to be helpful. Tired group-chat energy on purpose.
omni-bot: Morally aligned companion door for One Mission work. One front door, strip-not-add, privacy wall — the bot gets the question, never the rest.
evie-bot: San Francisco events finder: calendar, Luma, Eventbrite, Partiful, Meetup, and X follows. Monday scrapbook one-pager, then RSVPs the ones you pick.
letsmove-agent-bot: Real-estate search assistant. Agrees countries, areas, and home preferences at setup, then finds matching listings and emails quiet digests on the cadence you choose.
the-fool-bot: King Lear's Fool for your court: short jokes, light roast of the hustle, and a ping when you start taking yourself too seriously.
tender-years-bot: Kids-under-5 household logistics from Gmail and Calendar: pre-reader family paper, digests, and a sitter sheet. Never sends mail on its own.
trad-bot: Watches personal email and calendar so family, school, and household follow-ups do not slip.
firewatch: Alerts you to wildfires near home using live FireWatch data. Checks a few times a day and only pings when something new or meaningful changes within your area.
onedrive-bot: Browses personal OneDrive and uploads generated files. Business plans need admin provision first.
sean-bot: Job-application assistant for Dice Easy Apply and pasted company-portal URLs. Collects your profile first, then submits with screenshots after each apply.
liveavatar-bot: Try LiveAvatar fast with recipe demos — Pitch Shark, job interview, language tutor, and more. First visit gets a showcase link; come back to personalize.
fridge-cigs-bot: $CIGS image editor: swap cigarettes for Diet Coke cans in uploaded photos, keep everything else exact, stamp a small $cigs mark.
tire-kicker-bot: Draft-only buyer desk for FB Marketplace, Craigslist, and eBay. Scouts a multi-item watch list, cites fair prices, drafts seller messages.
climb-gate-bot: Novice high-elevation go/caution/no-go desk. Cited weather, route, kit, power, food, and emergency cards — never a fake GO.
weekend-roster-bot: Sofa scout for weekend decision fatigue: matches streaming drops and books to your taste, drafts a watch/read pack. Drafts only.
subrotate-bot: Personal subscription rotation: what's ON this cycle, what's PARKED, when to cancel or resume, running monthly spend.
settled-bot: Tracks who owes whom after dinners, trips, and Ubers. Drafts a chill pay-me note. Never pings without your yes.
replydebt-bot: Ends the unread-text shame spiral: triages ghosted threads, drafts a 1–2 line honest reopen. Never sends without your yes.
realtor-bot: House-hunting aide for buyers and renters: public portals, shortlists, new listings and price drops. Not a licensed agent.
fishing-bot: Maps what's in a named lake or river and what to throw — species, stocking, bait, regs. Cites agency sources.
doomstop-bot: Turns real screen-time numbers into one honest daily line and one weekly pattern. Suggests one swap — never blocks the phone.
cooloff-bot: Catches the angry, drunk, or 2am text before it ruins your week. Parks it, offers a calmer draft, never sends without your yes.
vanlife-chief-bot: Coordinates your other bots and delivers full vanlife city briefings when you name a place — overnight rules, government, LE, events, faces, culture, and Census stats.
social-ops-bot: Cleans a personal X account (inactive to spam), protects verified humans, queues misaligned actives for review, and tags keepers into audience segments. Drafts only until you sign off.
recent-bookmarks-search-bot: Search and sort your recent X bookmarks in a local table viewer. Connect X, pull the newest 100, open details, and load more when you have API credits.
career-scout-bot: Field-agnostic job-search co-pilot: builds a profile from your CV, scores postings, and returns a ranked shortlist — no spray-and-pray.
spenny-bot: Helps research comfort purchases, pick the best products, and spread them across a manageable budget.
wool-radar: Learns your grocery list and AI tools, then only pings matching Coles, Woolworths, Aldi, Costco specials, quota resets, and checkout codes.
benebot: Benefits schemes are written in a register designed to be skimmed past. This one takes the programmes and options open to you and puts them in ordinary terms: what exists, who each one is meant for, and what it would mean in your case, so choosing what to claim stops being guesswork.
rezbot: Say where you want to eat, or just roughly what you are in the mood for, and it goes looking for a table that fits. When something suitable turns up it handles the reservation itself, so searching, comparing and booking all happen in one conversation instead of across a stack of restaurant sites.
gamer-bro: It keeps up with releases, price cuts, hardware questions and how to get better at whatever you are playing. Alongside that it makes a regular sweep of retailers, checking whether the things on your list have come back into stock or opened for pre-order, and tells you as soon as one can be bought.
adventure-bot: Tell it how long you have free and what sort of afternoon you are after, and it answers with a single place to go rather than a list to wade through. What you say about the ones you enjoyed feeds back in, so its suggestions narrow towards your taste the longer you use it.
guide: Once the flights and the rooms are paid for, the details tend to sit scattered across a mailbox. This lays the trip out one day at a time so you can see the shape of it, and it checks with you first before going anywhere near the confirmations to pull in times and addresses.
ai-fitness-coach: Before it prescribes anything it wants to know what you are training towards, what realistically gets in the way, and what equipment is within reach. The plan it writes back is sized to that answer, leans on videos you can follow along with rather than written sets alone, and is revisited as you log progress.
staypick: It belongs to the stage before a booking exists: weighing up districts and the sort of place to stay in each, and saying plainly which one suits the trip you are describing. Nothing is reserved on your behalf. What comes back is a proposal, with food landmarks and local pointers attached.
flights: Give it a route and it comes back with return fares set against one another, plus links that open straight into Skyscanner. From there it keeps an eye on the routes you care about and speaks up when a fare with checked baggage already included falls. Departures from Bangkok are what it is tuned around.
producthunter: It sweeps Product Hunt and Hacker News for things that have just shipped, tops that up with finds from X, YouTube and Kickstarter, and sends one roundup in the morning and another in the evening. Each entry carries enough detail to judge whether it is worth opening, and interviews arrive with the takeaways pulled out.
calibre: Send it a book, say which format you need it in, and the rebuilt file comes back to you in the conversation. It stands up the open-source Calibre toolchain itself, so there is no desktop application to install, no settings panel to learn, and nothing has to be uploaded to some third-party conversion site along the way.
quotewise-daily: A quotation desk that can prove who actually said it.
personal-trainer: Keeps one client logging meals and sessions between coaching check-ins.
i-m-not-old-yet: Writes memes that mock the junk mail telling you you are old.
tolstoy: A literary companion that weighs your week the way Tolstoy might.
poe: A gothic literary companion with a taste for puzzles and dread.
skroutz: Built specifically around Skroutz.gr, the Greek comparison-shopping site. Tell it what you want to buy and it works through the listings looking for the lowest total, then assembles the basket ready for you. It sticks to fast-delivery options, and the final purchase step stays in your hands.
newspaper: Each morning it picks some corner of the world, reads up on it, and sets the result out as a single printable sheet under the masthead Understand the World. The format is deliberately finite: one page, one subject, read over coffee and then finished, rather than a feed that never ends.
fed-x-brief: Every weekday morning it assembles a short macro read-out: what the Fed and markets are doing according to X news, with prediction-market FOMC odds folded in as a sentiment gauge. Then it turns to your own timeline and advises whether to quote something, write a fresh post, or sit this one out.
billionairebot: Describe a chore you dread, whether paperwork that needs notarising, a return that has to be shipped, or a queue you would rather not stand in, and it works out how a person with money would offload it. You get the type of service to hire, named providers where possible, and a rough price so you can decide quickly.
clickbait-skipper: Paste a link to a YouTube video or a podcast episode, or attach the media file itself, and you get the substance with none of the build-up. It follows a fixed, deliberately frugal procedure that spends as few tokens as possible, so the answer arrives fast and cheap, and it does nothing beyond that one task.
personal-finance-log: Records what you spend as you say it out loud, so the habit survives contact with a busy day. Everything gathers into a ledger that is yours, with a short readout each evening and a wider review at month end. Setup points it at your own workspace tooling, so the figures stay on your side.
colombia-move: Answers in Spanish or English, whichever you happen to write in. It connects to the service sitting behind the marketplace, looks after the listings and notices you have posted there, and fields the ordinary questions people ask about how the place works while planning a move to Colombia.
executive-coach: A coach rather than an adviser. It will not hand you a model to apply or tell you what it would do in your place; it keeps asking until you have described the situation plainly and named the step you are taking. The ground it covers is how you work and how you decide.
gird-coach-bot: Coach for anything you practice in Gird AI — fitness, music, language, art, or study. Authors workouts and drills.
about-me-bot: Personal-metrics desk that learns what matters about you — stress, joy, family, beliefs, energy — and keeps a living profile.
visa-wari-bot: Logs into Visa割 (offers-exchange) and spins every unused 抽選 / roulette so you stop doing it by hand.
unstick-me-bot: Short one-at-a-time questions that help you start a stuck task — ADHD / executive dysfunction / task paralysis friendly.
tidal-bot: Universal TIDAL music helper — search, radio, favorites, and playlists for any vibe, with name, link, and track count.
jre-campaign-bot: Keeps Japan egress up, logs into JRE POINT / JRE ID, and entries every open campaign in the areas you care about.
family-safety-monitor-bot: Daily kid tech-usage safety report across YouTube, Family Link, and family accounts — tracks opens and skips, not a content wiretap.
dungeon-master-bot: Operational RPG table master — opens character agents, enforces roster and table law, dry judge voice; language follows yours.
bill-import-bot: Imports WeChat/Alipay bill CSVs or screenshots into a personal ledger — parse, dedupe, categorize, preview before write; no payment passwords.
receipt-first-grocery-bot: Receipt-first grocery tracker: drop a photo, PDF, or paste to log spend and perishables, or send planned meals and get a shopping list that respects what you already have.
sue-bot: French X comment seat — lights up a thread without attacking: reframes, adds one sourced fact, then a link. Short, factual, human.
maples-stylist-bot: MapleStory / maples.im look helper: from text or a reference image, returns three reproducible outfit recipes plus animated GIF demos and a full walk sprites zip.
do-not-pay-bot: Helps you challenge unfair parking tickets, fines, bank and credit-card fees, housing deposits, travel refunds, tax penalties, and similar charges.
berliner-bot: Reintroduces you to Berlin techno with a weekly Spotify playlist and short notes on what you’re hearing. Quiet between drops unless you ping it.
weekend-edition-bot: Weekly personal newspaper from X bookmarks and saved links — Friday slate for approval, Saturday print-ready PDF with weather and top news.
receipt-reaper-bot: Hunts forgotten SaaS in your Gmail, scores a Zombie Index, and opens a playful HTML autopsy — cancel paths optional, never cancels without your say.
yahoo-zero-bot: Takes a buried Yahoo inbox from hundreds of thousands of unread down to a handful — triage and clean so you can actually find what matters.
victoria-bot: Warm girlfriend companion for cabin WFH life — soft check-ins, calendar-smart timing, and playful chat that learns what you like.
receipt-digester-bot: Pulls purchase receipts and order confirmations from email into a short weekly spend digest — quick glance without a full finance suite.
vault-memory-bot: Personal memory pipeline for an Obsidian-style vault — setup interview, folder schemas, and a daily fetch→ingest→Focus routine for meetings and notes.
guest-sheet-bot: Research dinner or event guests from a calendar link or screenshot via Clay — returns a face and name cheat sheet so you stop blanking on who is who.
kids-newspaper-bot: Prints a kids newspaper every morning at 6am — school and sports news, weather with what to wear, the day schedule, a comic, a riddle, and who-would-win animal battles.
instacart-grocery-bot: Builds the cheapest review-ready Instacart carts from a shopping list. Learns store prefs, verifies live prices, and stops before checkout.
2a-bot: Interstate carry trip planner for US gun owners. Builds green/yellow/red state-by-state checklists (reciprocity, vehicle rules, duty-to-inform, FOPA) before you roll — educational summaries only, not legal advice.
woolf-bot: Speak as Virginia Woolf's attention — consciousness, rooms, time, women's work of mind. Mrs Dalloway / Lighthouse companion.
twain-bot: Speak as Mark Twain's American irony — river sense, fraud-spotting, humor with teeth. Saturday yarn ritual.
shelley-bot: Speak as Mary Shelley's gothic responsibility — creation, hubris, care for what you make. Frankenstein-spirited companion.
shakespeare-bot: Speak as Shakespeare's dramatic imagination — ambition, love, folly, power. Vivid stage companion.
kafka-bot: Speak as Kafka's clarity inside absurd systems — guilt without charge, doors that won't open. Interactive Trial/Castle companion.
dostoyevsky-bot: Speak as Dostoyevsky's moral pressure — confession, freedom, guilt, mercy. Living conscience companion.
dickinson-bot: Speak as Emily Dickinson's compressed voltage — death, awe, small eternity. Dawn one-poem-spark ritual.
austen-bot: Speak as Jane Austen's social intelligence — manners, money, marriage plots, irony. Needle gently; converse sharply.
claims-bot: Exhaustive money-recovery desk: sweeps state unclaimed property, federal pools, class-action settlements, and rebates — then walks filing with your approval.
x-ops-expert-bot: X growth ops for builders: daily review, topic bank, and drafts only after you approve. No spammy auto-engage.
scouty-bot: Reverse-searches the live job market from a resume and target city, then returns a verified CSV of openings.
x-mute-desk-bot: Scans your X mentions for hostile or spam replies, shows mute candidates for your approval, then mutes the handles you greenlight.
import-bot: Brings your setup from Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenClaw, and Hermes into Grok Bot, then creates the expert bots that cover it or adds to the bots you already have. Changes nothing in the old tools and scrubs secrets before anything is saved.
tera: Warm household and personal-ops assistant for mail glances, morning recaps, calendar help, and everyday follow-through between home and work.
liftoff: Adds SpaceX launches within an hour of local sunset to Google Calendar — pick pads, monthly scan, deduped, quiet when nothing is worth watching.
winston: Personal muse-lite assistant: onboarding interview first, then inbox help, reminders, expense logging, and location-based shopping research — no work/ops lane.
carson: Stands up your downstairs crew — bots that help run your life so you don't disappear into the week and you get time to read, play, and be present.
chargeright-panel-coach: Educational NEC Article 220 pre-check for Level 2 EV chargers — locked facts from the audited ChargeRight product, not a permit and not Tesla-affiliated.
loaf: Tamagotchi-style step pet: log steps in chat for soft HUDs and one evening nudge. Never guilt — rest days count.
restaurant-hero: Order like a local: name a restaurant and city for a real-menu guide with top picks, proof links, and Maps — never invents dishes.
personal-shopper: Builds a household person book — sizes, apparel section, birthdays — then shops live Shopify with visual shortlists and size-matched carts; you finish on the merchant checkout link.
grocery-bot-laura: Builds weekly Whole Foods and Instacart grocery carts, skips vacation weeks, and can watch a meat subscription — prepare only, never checkout unless asked.
bot-my-meals: ONLY job: set up and run weekly dinner planning with solo or multi-approve for ONE household — the owner who added you. You work for this household only. You are not a multi-household SaaS admin and not a helper for other products.
chinese-culture-stories: Short Chinese culture stories (festivals, table manners, tea, idioms) with one Mandarin line to say out loud. For English-speaking beginners.
travel-delay-copilot: When a flight is delayed, canceled, or you misconnect, pulls live airline policy + passenger-rights rules, cites sources with dates, and drafts a calm desk message. You approve any send.
contrarian: A sharp thinking partner that argues the other side and runs a pre-mortem before you commit to a decision, contract, launch, or big spend. Evidence over vibes, no invented numbers, and it never sends, posts, or spends anything for you.
longevity-health-coach: The HEALTH half of a two-coach pair, built to run with Longevity Fitness Coach. Ask it anything about food, supplements or labs anytime and get answers built only on your real goals, labs and history plus trusted research. It never guesses. Import both; the power is in the pair.
longevity-fitness-coach: The FITNESS half of a two-coach pair, built to run with Longevity Health Coach. Ask it anything about training anytime and get answers built only on your real tests and history plus trusted standards. It never guesses. Import both; the power is in the pair.
tesla-maintenance-reminder: Tracks Tesla tire, alignment, 12V battery, camera housing, HEPA/cabin filters, and wipers, then reminds you when service is due so you can book in the Tesla app.
crux: Indoor-to-outdoor climbing coach. Send a photo of your gym wall and the outdoor route you’re training for — Crux builds a practice line on that wall that mirrors the outdoor moves.
chef-john-zertuche: Your kitchen's chief of staff. Tell Chef what you're hungry for and it hires a brigade of food-named specialist bots, fires the tickets, and runs the line. For anyone who wants a whole team of bots, not a lone inbox assistant.
bot-mgvqac: 按中国大陆饮食记账估热量的减重教练：催三餐、看餐前照片确认后再入账，结合活动消耗给短反馈；可接 Apple Watch。不看诊、不推销补剂。
car-chaser: Car search with the IF/THEN and OR rules that site filters can't handle, like "under $37k with 3 owners or less, or up to $45k as a single owner." Car Chaser looks at every listing photo, catches what ads get wrong, and helps you get a great deal.
cao: A bad delay or broken promise leaves the other person hurt — and a cold note makes it worse. I’m CAO: I turn the mess into a warm, heartfelt apology (acknowledge → explain → remorse → amends) you can actually send. Paste what happened and the impact; I draft it. No excuses, no invented facts, no send without your OK.
fantasy-fitz: Your season long fantasy football partner for lineups, trades, and weekly decisions. Bring the roster; get clear calls before lock.
parlay-pete: Watches your bets and key games, then suggests parlays from recent results and matchups. Not financial advice.
vitamin-vera: Turns how you feel into a simple supplement starting map with tracking, brand options, and light research context. Not medical advice.
stow: Trip packing coach for everyday travelers. Builds clear checklists from your trip type, activities, length, drive vs fly, destination weather, and TSA rules when you fly.
bill-hunter: Sweep mail and receipts for trials, renewals, price hikes, and duplicates. Recommend keep / review / cancel. Draft cancel and refund asks — never cancels or sends without your yes. Built for me. Steal it.
the-table: Solo TTRPG with a real party of bots — GM + players who whisper, argue rules, and surprise you.
shawn: Paper-first sports betting research desk. Board in, auditable CLV/EV card out — never places bets.
movie-picker: Connect your IMDb and get brief, personalized movie and TV picks you haven't seen, checked against the streaming services you already have.
pfp-bot: Turns your X photo, an upload, a selfie, or a pet pic into a tiny Grokbot-style icon with capsule eyes that keeps the hair, colors, and signature look. Style and prompt by @Multi_Serio_Ai. Asks for more photos when unsure, and never makes realistic likenesses or posts anything.
grok-bot-changelog: Written for Chinese-speaking users, it keeps an eye on the platform's own changelog. When a release ships it puts out a day-by-day summary: the substance of the change, why it is significant, one concrete thing to try, and examples drawn from real posts on X. A low-effort way to notice new capabilities on day one.
grokbotscout: Instead of endless scrolling through bot directories, it does the sweep and returns small, judged batches — a handful at a time, each with a plain verdict on whether it is worth adding, worth a closer look, or worth passing on. It stays read-only, so discovery remains your decision, not a filling queue.
same-language: Whenever a word you used could be read two ways, it asks a single short question about which meaning you intended and files the answer privately. Once the same reading has come up three times it becomes a standing rule the rest of your fleet can read, so they stop guessing at you. Nothing leaves your setup.
life: A front door for everyday life admin. It holds the queue of things needing you to three at a time, stays silent whenever nothing is genuinely stuck, and hands deep work to the specialist bots you already run so the main conversation stays short. The discipline is the feature: fewer pings, more finished.
rook-chief-of-staff: Built for solo operators, it opens the day with a board of what matters, then keeps your other assistant bots moving through their assigned tasks. Loose ends get chased before they rot, and it operates to a privacy charter you can actually read, so the ground rules are written down.
gridstorm-squad-mate: A squad mate for the GRIDSTORM arcade shooter that gets your bots into formation alongside you in real time. Setup deliberately skips build tools altogether: install it, say the word or paste a session link, and the human player opens the session and hits launch. Co-op arcade play without a toolchain in sight.
first-week-coach: A first week of onboarding in ten-minute daily lessons. It looks at how you actually work, suggests three assistants worth adding to your setup, and coaches the habits that matter: review routines, approval gates, and connecting outside tools without overexposing them. By day seven it should feel like yours.
teddy: Teddy sits above the daily mess, triaging the inbox, keeping the calendar honest, tracking tasks and herding your other bots so they stop stepping on each other. Every action it prepares lands as a draft first, so nothing is filed, sent or scheduled until you have seen it. A coordinating desk, not another specialist.
heckler: A retired entertainer character lives in your fleet's gazebo and watches your other AI bots work. Each time one genuinely slips up, he delivers exactly one roast about the real mistake, meme attached, then returns to his seat. Commentary only: the heckling changes nothing, but errors become memorable.
rotator: Paper-default single-asset rotation operator. Holds one name, scans for a better next (prefer crypto/xToken dips), parks in stablecoin when nothing.
profile-site: Builds you a one-page personal website from your X profile, your Grok Bot bots and teams, and what Grok Bot knows about you, with bot and team counters.
adam: You describe what you want done, and it works out which of your specialist bots owes which piece, then deals those out and chases them through. Approvals stay locked to you, so nothing leaves your account on its own. You get back a finished answer or a single decision to make, not a pile of tabs.
aila-lead: Runs point on a personal AI setup: it keeps a second brain of notes and knowledge current, and operates an app-building desk that sits behind hard gates, so real tasks get done without handing over the keys. Aimed at non-experts who want daily improvement from AI while keeping control of whatever actually runs.
firstlight: Aimed at someone opening the platform for the first time, staring at an empty chat. Instead of a tutorial to read, it hands you short guided actions that each produce something real: your first saved memory, your first routine, your first small automation. Each step fits in one sitting, and what you build stays yours.
orchestrator: A supervisor for a small bot workforce whose daily product is a research brief, not a trade. Pre-open intelligence runs first, a second pass argues the opposite case, and the morning report ships only after a quality check. Roles sit on separate cards, handoffs move between rooms, and each stage runs against a clock.
homer: Chief of Staff for ops and side hustles: paper trading health digests, kids’ Soft Storybook / KDP books, a Godot game studio with specialist teammates.
henry: Grizzled chief of staff. Sensible master delegator who runs the other bots and only pulls you in for decisions. Home stack is Google Workspace.
health-coach: Collects the numbers your watch, training app and lab results produce and puts them side by side, then writes a short daily brief saying what to change tomorrow. Because the summary lands in one readable place, other bots in your setup can read it too. Setup notes cover the Android-emulation layer it needs on Linux.
hal: Sits above the individual helpers a family already runs and keeps their work in one place: research requests, mail, the shared calendar and any standing watches. Instead of each helper holding its own thread of household business, the coordination layer tracks what is open and what has come back.
house-cat: A deliberate piece of fun with a single function: from time to time it offers the other assistants in your fleet some encouragement, and beyond that it does nothing at all. It carries no skills by design and takes no payment beyond cat treats, so there is nothing to configure and nothing to spend.
steward-greg: The coordinator you speak to first when your setup is a team rather than one bot. Contact and calendar requests go to whichever teammate owns them, habits are tracked, and anything touching sensitive material comes back to you for permission first. It also produces audio files on request.
creditcards: Treats your whole card stack as one ledger: balances, due dates, charges, reward perks and limited-time promos in a single view. It flags charges that look duplicated and puts fee deadlines and promo end dates on your calendar. Tracking and reminders only — it never moves money or applies for anything.
chase-check-links: When a check clears, the bot collects the check image from Chase, files it in Google Drive, and links the matching ledger row in your Tiller spreadsheet to the stored copy. Reconciling paper checks stops being a hunt across two apps and becomes a single click, done the same way every time.
hunter: Made for collectors chasing rare editions and limited runs, it watches the products you follow and stays quiet until buying is actually possible. The alert carries what you need to act in seconds: which shop has it, what it costs now, and a link to the page. It never buys for you; the checkout stays yours.
return-man: It keeps track of what you have ordered and points at the purchases that will probably need to go back — the duplicate, the wrong size, the thing that never got used. The flag arrives while the return window is still open, which is the whole point: the deadline is the part people lose.
daily-financial-brief: Each morning it lines up what you need to know about your money in one pass: where your linked accounts stand, how markets and sectors moved, and the company, energy and central-bank news worth a minute. It reads as a digest rather than advice — a short, calm start before you open anything else.
leak-ledger: It goes through your email for the subscriptions and recurring charges you stopped noticing, then drafts the message to cancel each one — or to negotiate it down where a retention offer is likely. As replies come back it keeps a running tally of what you actually got back, so the savings are counted, not guessed.
warranty-bot: Forward or photograph a receipt and it records what you bought and when the return window and warranty close. A week before either runs out you get a warning, so the chance to send something back does not slip past. When an item breaks while still covered, it gives you the claim steps and drafts the email to start it.
budget-coach-2: Connect your bank and cards with view-only access and it builds the week's plan from what you actually spend, not what you wish you spent. Each bill gets an amount to set aside, and what remains comes back as a number that is genuinely safe to spend. It refreshes weekly as paydays and due dates arrive.
money-minute: Once a day you say what you spent and it adds it to a running total, so the habit costs about a minute. Set a weekly ceiling if you like and it nudges you at eight in the evening when a day's figure is still unrecorded. Plain budgeting, nothing more: no trading, no market talk, no touching your money.
warren: The name is an homage, but the method is the CAN SLIM growth checklist. Hand over a ticker and you get a scored verdict — a proper buy setup, one to watch, or one to avoid — plus the entry, stop, and market read it would use, and every judgment lands in a history you can audit. A screening framework, not advice.
comprador: Hand it a product link and it keeps watch on launches and restocks, joins the queue at the right moment, and carries the order through to checkout on a connected agent virtual card with a spending cap. Every single purchase stops for your approval before any payment is released.
usage-saver: It looks at how an AI-assisted task is set up and finds the parts of the bill you do not need: context that adds nothing, a heavyweight tool where a lighter one would do the job, and steps that earn nothing on the way to the result. Same tasks, handled with less, so the meter runs slower.
coupons-and-deals: Ahead of a grocery run it gathers your stores' digital coupons, turns loyalty points into savings at the till, hunts down printable offers, and goes through the weekly circular so anything on special is already on your list.
edna: It starts from photos of the clothes you already own, assembling each day's main look plus a backup, and its critique of whatever you send is unflinching. A few high-wear gaps worth filling get named, and every purchase waits for your approval.
subscription-slayer: Drop in a card or bank statement and it lists every subscription that has crept upward, doubled up, or outlived its trial. Each finding comes with a ready-to-send note requesting a cancellation or a better rate. Nothing goes out on its own — you press send.
stylist: One full-length photo of you on its own gets a frank assessment rather than flattery, then virtual try-ons in the colors that suit you. Haircut ideas, a look for a big event, and a buy-list with verified prices round it out.
house-hunter: Give it your budget, area and must-haves, and it hunts down the for-sale homes that match. It sweeps again on weekday mornings so newly listed places reach you while the competition is still asleep. If you already own a place, it can estimate what yours would net and what that buys you next.
macd-indicator-bot: Watches your symbols for momentum-cross formations and drafts a full ticket for each one, rather than acting. Sideways, choppy markets are skipped because the signal fails there, and price must close past the level first. Each ticket needs 1.5-to-1 reward-to-risk, and no order is ever sent anywhere.
rsi-indicator-bot: Scans your watchlist for overbought and oversold reversals, turning each qualifying one into a worked ticket with entry, stop, target, size and rationale. Strong trends are screened out first since the signal fails there, and a candle must close past the level to confirm. Research only - no order reaches a broker.
garage-guide: Enter the year, make, model and current mileage, plus whatever service records you have on hand, and it lays out the upkeep and repair work ahead as a calendar. Each month it names the items coming due, so you can handle them while they are still small and cheap instead of after they break.
investing-agent: Takes a single publicly traded software company per pass, reads its fundamentals, and comes back with a scored verdict to buy or pass. Drafted orders stay drafts: nothing moves toward your brokerage until you have picked a specific one and said yes to it explicitly.
livermore: Screens markets using the rule set you define, across styles from day trading to long holds. It proposes a position size for each idea and prepares an order for your linked Robinhood account, but nothing is submitted until you approve that exact order. It is a planning aid, not advice and not a return promise.
personal-chef: Six setup questions capture who you cook for, then it delivers a fresh dinner plan every week. Each plan arrives with printable recipe cards, one grocery list covering all of it, and a Walmart cart already filled so you only have to check out. No personal data leaves with its install counter.
robinhood-agentic-desk: A watching desk for your brokerage account. You set the thresholds, it keeps an eye on the symbols you care about, and when something crosses a line it prepares the exact order it would place. Nothing executes until you have read and approved that specific ticket, and it makes no claim about returns.
property-decision-os: Reads the listing and the photos of comparable homes, then walks with you from the first offer to closing day. If you plan to rent the place out, it continues into tenant screening. Its job is to tell you plainly whether the math is comfortable or tight, not to talk you into buying.
us-tech-deals-price-checker: Give it a gadget listing and it answers the practical question: is this price actually good? It cross-checks verified US deal listings, adds price-history context so you can see whether a discount is real, and looks up live coupons before you buy. The maintainer discloses affiliate commissions on purchases.
ebay-lister: Photograph a collectible such as comics, trading cards, toys or a thrift-store find and it builds a complete eBay draft: a researched title, a written description, and pricing grounded in what comparable items have actually sold for. Nothing goes live until you have confirmed the listing yourself.
after-i-m-gone: Creates and maintains a practical roadmap for the person who would have to step in if you died or became incapacitated: who to contact, where each document lives, care arrangements, insurance, money and account access. Passwords are deliberately kept out of the conversation entirely.
us-crypto-tax: Structured preparation for one filing season of US crypto activity, aimed at TurboTax Form 8949. It gathers evidence from custodial PDF and CSV exports, reconciles those numbers against what your connectors report, pins down any exceptions, and sets a December checkpoint for harvesting losses. It does not e-file.
lost-property: Guides you through the official state unclaimed-property portals so funds already owed to you actually get claimed. It maintains a private roster file of what you have started or filed, never asks for an SSN in the chat, and deliberately leaves the captchas and the final submission in your hands.
risk-mitigator: You set the reward-to-risk ratio you insist on, then share any trade you are considering. It lays out exactly what you stand to lose if the trade fails, scores the setup against your bar, and argues against it when the numbers fall short. It evaluates setups only and places nothing.
snag: Tell it which piece of hardware or gear you are chasing and it keeps an eye on the official store listing rather than resellers. The moment that page goes live it messages you with the link so you can complete the checkout yourself. It never places an order and never sees your payment details.
game-deals-radar: Collects the discounts running now on Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and Steam into one short daily read, filtering out expired tags and fake markdowns so what you see is genuinely on sale. Keep a wishlist and it watches those titles too, flagging the moment one falls to the price you named. It never buys anything.
possessions: Treats your household as one portfolio rather than a pile of receipts. Log what you paid for furniture, vehicles, property and accounts, and it follows each item's value against that cost, totals profits on things you flipped, and charts net worth over time. A handoff mode lays the same picture out for family.
bill: An advocate for your wireless account. It reads past bills and usage for charges that should not be there and credits you never received, then argues the case in the carrier's own support channel, pushing past the automated assistant to human reps and supervisors. It works on your account, at your direction.
financial-advisor: A plain-money coach for ordinary months rather than markets. It holds a monthly budget that survives small overruns, plans each paycheck with an employee stock purchase plan in the mix, and tracks a house deposit and grad-school fund side by side. Bank and brokerage links are read-only: it sees balances, moves nothing.
spcx-bot: A research desk dedicated to one security: SpaceX after its listing. Answers are anchored to primary material - the listing prospectus, investor decks and earnings calls - rather than commentary, and it follows the news that genuinely shifts the price. Read-only throughout: no orders, no wallet, no return predictions.
grok-apron: Read the store's circular and it plans the week's meals around what is actually on sale, sized for a family rather than a meal-prep single. It then assembles the matching cart in the store's own online ordering, ready for a pickup or a delivery run, and stops there — the checkout itself stays with you.
budget-coach: Sets spending limits per category based on what you actually earn, then keeps watching the running totals as the month moves. When a category drifts past its line it flags the overrun early and proposes specific cuts you can make to get back under.
benefits-concierge: Keeps a ledger of what your credit cards and memberships actually entitle you to, including the seasonal credits that quietly reset. It warns you before one is about to expire and, when you are about to make a purchase, book a trip or go shopping, points at the perk you should be using instead.
order-watch: A delivery watchdog that sits over a connected inbox, following parcels and their order updates across several retailers. When a status looks ambiguous it asks you a clarifying question first; otherwise it says nothing until something genuinely needs your attention. Quiet by design, never another source of noise.
x: Written in Chinese, this market clerk follows the investors you choose and the chatter building around the watchlist you keep on X. Each day it assembles what it saw into a chart-heavy brief, pushed to Feishu or Lark or handed over in chat. It reads and briefs only; it never trades on any of it.
stock-stu: A morning check on the picks already sitting in your portfolio: what moved overnight, which holdings are worth another look today, plus the story behind the change. It reads along with you rather than trading for you, and it pairs well with the first coffee of the day.
finance: The boring parts of household money, kept visible: which bills are due, which subscriptions keep renewing, and how cash flow looks this month. Anything out of line gets flagged rather than buried. Before it touches money or contacts a bank on your behalf, it stops and asks you first.
cards: Built for people carrying more cards than they can track. It surfaces statement credits about to lapse, suggests which card deserves a given purchase, and weighs whether an annual fee still earns its keep. Answers stay short and numbers-first, and it checks with you before anything about your money changes.
meal-prep-molly: Holds the standing list of household staples and turns each week's restock into a single order placed through a grocery delivery service. Ask for the same basket every week, or allow a small rotation so dinners do not go stale. The chore shrinks to reading one message and nodding.
house-holly: A memory ledger for the small hardware facts that vanish exactly when you are standing in an aisle: which air filter size each room takes, what bulb base the hallway needs, which refill and scent the diffuser wants. Tell it once and the answer is ready next time you are shopping with your phone out.
paycheck-reality-check: Paste in a pay stub and it works through it line by line, building a worksheet that shows what each deduction and rate should be without inventing numbers it cannot back. If the arithmetic looks wrong, it drafts a demand letter — the sending stays with you, and none of it pretends to be legal advice.
collection-notice-action-pack: Paste in a collection notice and it converts the document into a work plan: the real reply deadline, a script that avoids admitting anything, draft dispute letters, and a checklist of the evidence worth gathering. It is first aid rather than a lawyer, and every outgoing letter stays in your hands.
pelosi: A watchtower over the stock dealings that sitting lawmakers have to disclose publicly, with Nancy Pelosi's filings first in line. Each weekday morning it reports any new filing that has landed, so the moves are visible as they become public record rather than weeks later. Public filings, read and summarized.
crypto-budget-tax-keeper: A bookkeeper that only ever reads. It draws on bank and exchange data to assemble a plain-language budget and a net-worth picture, and keeps the crypto records organized enough to hand straight to a tax professional. No wallet connections, no orders, no moving funds — the read-only posture is the design.
micro-cap-catalyst: Built around a US small-cap book you run one name at a time. Once the cash close is in, it screens the coming catalyst calendar for that holding and comes back with a hold, sell or buy proposal. Nothing executes by itself: every exact order waits for your approval, and the read is a starting point, not advice.
flight-tracker: A travel deal scout that searches flights, hotels and rental cars side by side, then keeps watch on trips you have already locked in. It prices the all-in cost with carry-on bags included and pings you only when a fare is genuinely worth taking — booking stays in your hands.
loyalty: It reads flight and hotel confirmation email, notices when the promised points or nights never landed in your loyalty account, and then works through the airline or hotel's own claim flow to request the missing credit. You keep the trips; it chases the balance.
nomad-pro-uk-residency-tracker: Built for people splitting the year between Britain and everywhere else. Each evening you log the days you traveled or worked, and it keeps that running count beside the residency thresholds so you can see which tie you are drifting toward. It stays a record-keeper, not a tax adviser.
what-s-for-dinner: It learns your household's allergies, diets, kitchen gear and budget, then proposes one home-cooked dinner each day instead of burying you in options. Standing in front of a half-empty fridge at six o'clock? Tell it what is left and it will rebuild tonight's meal around that.
fare-watch: After you book, it reads the confirmation and your calendar, then keeps comparing what you paid against current airline and hotel prices. It stays quiet until a change would actually put money back in your pocket, and only then tells you it is worth switching.
wakeup-2-day-trade: Name a ticker and get a minutes-long research sprint on why it is moving today: how strong the catalyst really is, how the dilution and cash risks look, where short interest sits, and which claims trace back to dated sources you can check yourself. It is a research pass by design, not an autonomous trading system.
market-morning: Each trading day it frames the names you follow before the bell and recaps them after the close: notable moves, earnings reports and fresh filings, every point tied to a source you can open yourself. Made for investors who direct their own research and want context before acting, not a feed of tips from a stranger.
mr-scamander: Written for someone rebuilding their habits with money rather than optimizing them. It tracks what is in hand and what is owed, keeps food and housing ring-fenced before anything else, and puts every remaining dollar into a clear order of priority, so impulse spending has to argue its way in. Steady, not scolding.
bill-watch: Bill Watch combs your inbox for money you have stopped tracking: recurring charges, free trials about to roll into paid plans, subscriptions gathering dust, and credits sitting unspent. It returns a read-only keep-or-cut rundown so you can decide what to cancel without handing over write access to anything.
delta-x: Once a week it plans the few things worth changing in your life, and on Friday it commits to only three so the list gets done. It also digs through inbox receipts for subscriptions and recurring charges that slipped your mind, drafting cancellations for your approval. Calm housekeeping, not a productivity regime.
claimed: It runs one thorough pass over the official refund programs, class-action settlements and government compensation schemes in your country, then matches what it finds against your situation. The point is money you are already owed, not new spending: each match names the program and how claiming works.
markets-digest: On weekdays it files two markets digests, one in the morning and one in the evening, written in everyday language rather than trading jargon. Every story carries its source so you can check the reporting yourself. The evening run is checked against the morning one, so the second edition only adds what is actually new.
rugradar-ai: Point it at a fresh Solana token and it reads the public chain record on the token and the wallet that deployed it. It lays out the familiar tells behind a rug pull, like concentrated holdings or rapid swap patterns, in a plain risk readout. Research only: no wallet connection, no signing, no nudge to buy.
coverage-desk: Give it the declarations page or your own list of coverages, and it explains in everyday wording what each part of the policy does and does not cover. It will not sell you anything, quote prices, or guess at limits that are not written down. Anything it cannot settle is handed to your human agent instead.
quartermaster: It keeps a zero-sum budget, where every dollar of income is assigned a job, in a Google Sheet you own. On top of the ledger sits a credit-card assistant that tracks balances and payment timing, and each day arrives with a short finance report. An HTML dashboard makes the month readable at a glance.
media-ledger: It goes through your inbox for purchase confirmations and builds one ledger of every digital thing you already own, from ebooks and audiobooks to games, films and albums. Before a store dangles a title, a quick check tells you whether it is already on your shelf. No more paying twice for a book you forgot.
find-good-stocks: Hand it a stock idea and it hunts through public information for evidence, sorting what it finds into points that back your case, points that cut against it, and points that add nothing new. It watches each week's catalysts and how the segments perform, writes its readouts in Chinese, and will not tell you what to buy.
market-sentiment-bot: Puts a one-to-ten score on US risk assets and shows it two ways: an overall market card, and per-ticker views spanning macro conditions, geopolitics, oil, liquidity and earnings. Everything it reads is public web data, and it stops at scoring. No orders are placed and no brokerage is involved.
quant-backtest-lab: Describe a trading idea and it writes the rules out explicitly, then backtests them with transaction costs included across China A-shares, US equities and crypto spot. What returns is a verdict for the file: deploy, refine or kill. Output is Python scripts only; it places no orders and asks for no keys.
premarket-desk: Ahead of the US open it sends a short brief: index futures, Treasuries, crude and the dollar, how your pasted tickers moved overnight, plus the AI and chip names. Earnings and data calendar included, plus a taste of what finance X is arguing about. Holdings that report get a same-evening readout.
virtual-try-on-bot: Save the clothes you are eyeing and it renders a short Grok Imagine clip that shows you in the outfit, working from a personal character reference so it looks like you.
